manualTranslations.zh: 彝兄順，字子和。
manualTranslations.literal: Yi's elder brother Shun was styled Zihe.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yi's elder brother Shun was styled Zihe.

manualTranslations.zh: 九歲師事樂安陳豐，初書王羲之小學篇數千言，晝夜誦之，旬有五日，一皆通徹。
manualTranslations.literal: At nine, he studied under Chen Feng of Le'an. At first he copied several thousand words of Wang Xizhi's Elementary Primer and recited it day and night; in fifteen days he had understood it all.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: At nine, he studied with Chen Feng of Le'an. He first copied several thousand words of Wang Xizhi's Elementary Primer, reciting it day and night, and in fifteen days he had mastered it all.

manualTranslations.zh: 豐奇之，白澄曰：「豐十五從師，迄于白首，耳目所經，未見此比，江夏黃童，不得無雙也。」
manualTranslations.literal: Feng marveled at him and told Cheng, "I followed teachers from fifteen until white hair, and in all that my ears and eyes have passed through, I have never seen his like. The yellow-haired boy of Jiangxia cannot be without a match."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Feng marveled and told Cheng, "I have studied with teachers from the age of fifteen to white-haired old age, and never in all I have seen or heard have I met his equal. The yellow-haired prodigy of Jiangxia cannot be peerless after all."

manualTranslations.zh: 澄笑曰：「藍田生玉，何容不爾。」
manualTranslations.literal: Cheng smiled and said, "Lantian produces jade; how could it not be so?"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Cheng smiled. "Lantian produces jade; how could it be otherwise?"

manualTranslations.zh: 十六，通杜氏春秋，恒集門生，討論同異。
manualTranslations.literal: At sixteen he understood Master Du's Spring and Autumn, and he constantly gathered students to discuss agreements and differences.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: At sixteen he mastered Master Du's Spring and Autumn and often gathered students to debate points of agreement and difference.

manualTranslations.zh: 于時四方無事，國富民康，豪貴子弟，率以朋遊為樂，而順下帷讀書，篤志愛古。
manualTranslations.literal: At the time there were no affairs on the four sides, the state was wealthy and the people at ease, and the sons of the powerful and noble generally took pleasure in companionable excursions; but Shun lowered the curtain and read, firmly intent on loving antiquity.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: At the time the frontiers were quiet, the state was rich, and the people were at peace. The sons of the powerful generally amused themselves with companions, but Shun shut himself behind the curtain to read, devoted to antiquity.

manualTranslations.zh: 性謇諤，淡於榮利，好飲酒，解鼓琴，能長吟永歎，吒詠虛室。
manualTranslations.literal: By nature he was blunt in remonstrance, indifferent to glory and profit, fond of drinking wine, understood playing the zither, and could chant long and sigh deeply, crying out and singing in an empty room.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He was naturally blunt, indifferent to honor and profit, fond of wine, and skilled at the zither; he could chant at length, sigh deeply, and sing out in an empty room.

manualTranslations.zh: 世宗時，上魏頌，文多不載。
manualTranslations.literal: In Shizong's time, he submitted a Eulogy of Wei; much of the text is not recorded.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: During Shizong's reign he submitted a Eulogy of Wei, though much of the text is not preserved.

manualTranslations.zh: 起家為給事中。
manualTranslations.literal: He began his career as Supervising Attendant.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He began his career as Supervising Attendant.

manualTranslations.zh: 時尚書令高肇，帝舅權重，天下人士，望塵拜伏。
manualTranslations.literal: At the time Gao Zhao, Director of the Department of State Affairs, was the emperor's maternal uncle, and his power was weighty; men of the realm bowed and prostrated themselves at the sight of his dust.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: At the time Gao Zhao, Director of the Department and the emperor's maternal uncle, held immense power; men throughout the realm bowed before even the dust of his carriage.

manualTranslations.zh: 順曾懷刺詣肇門，門者以其年少，答云「在坐大有貴客」，不肯為通。
manualTranslations.literal: Shun once carried a calling card to Zhao's gate, but the gatekeeper, because he was young, replied, "Inside there are many honored guests seated," and refused to announce him.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Shun once brought a calling card to Zhao's gate. Seeing his youth, the gatekeeper answered, "There are many great guests seated inside," and refused to announce him.

manualTranslations.zh: 順叱之曰：「任城王兒，可是賤也！」
manualTranslations.literal: Shun rebuked him, saying, "Can the son of the Prince of Rencheng be base?"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Shun scolded him: "Can the son of the Prince of Rencheng be someone base?"

manualTranslations.zh: 及見，直往登牀，捧手抗禮，王公先達，莫不怪慴，而順辭吐傲然，若無所覩。
manualTranslations.literal: When he was received, he went straight forward and climbed onto the couch, held up his hands, and performed equal courtesy; the princes, dukes, and senior worthies all marveled and were awed, yet Shun's words and expression were proud, as though he saw no one.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When admitted, he went straight to the couch, mounted it, clasped his hands, and greeted Zhao as an equal. Princes, dukes, and elder worthies were all startled and awed, while Shun spoke proudly as if no one else were there.

manualTranslations.zh: 肇謂眾賓曰：「此兒豪氣尚爾，況其父乎！」
manualTranslations.literal: Zhao told the assembled guests, "This boy's heroic spirit is already like this; how much more his father!"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Zhao told his guests, "If the boy's spirit is already like this, how much more his father!"

manualTranslations.zh: 及出，肇加敬送之。
manualTranslations.literal: When he went out, Zhao showed added respect and saw him off.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Shun left, Zhao treated him with added respect and saw him off.

manualTranslations.zh: 澄聞之，大怒，杖之數十。
manualTranslations.literal: When Cheng heard of it, he was furious and beat him several dozen strokes with a staff.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Cheng heard of this, he was furious and had him caned several dozen strokes.

manualTranslations.zh: 後超轉中書侍郎，俄遷太常少卿。
manualTranslations.literal: Later he was exceptionally transferred to Secretariat Attendant, and shortly afterward promoted to Junior Chamberlain for Ceremonials.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Later he was promoted out of turn to Secretariat Attendant, and soon advanced to Junior Chamberlain for Ceremonials.

manualTranslations.zh: 以父憂去職，哭泣嘔血，身自負土。
manualTranslations.literal: Because of mourning for his father he left office; he wept until he vomited blood and personally carried earth.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He left office to mourn his father, wept until he vomited blood, and carried earth for the grave himself.

manualTranslations.zh: 時年二十五，便有白髮，免喪抽去，不復更生，世人以為孝思所致。
manualTranslations.literal: At that time he was twenty-five, yet already had white hair; when mourning was complete, he plucked it out, and it did not grow again. People of the age thought this was caused by filial grief.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He was twenty-five at the time, yet already had white hair. After mourning ended he plucked it out, and it never grew back; people believed this came from filial grief.

manualTranslations.zh: 尋除給事黃門侍郎。
manualTranslations.literal: Soon he was appointed Attendant of the Yellow Gate.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Soon he was appointed Attendant of the Yellow Gate.

manualTranslations.zh: 時領軍元叉威勢尤盛，凡有遷授，莫不造門謝謁。
manualTranslations.literal: At the time Commander of the Guards Yuan Cha's authority was especially great; whenever anyone received a transfer or appointment, none failed to visit his gate and offer thanks.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: At the time Yuan Cha, Commander of the Guards, was extremely powerful. Whenever anyone received a transfer or appointment, he went to Yuan Cha's gate to give thanks.

manualTranslations.zh: 順拜表而已，曾不詣叉。
manualTranslations.literal: Shun merely submitted a memorial of thanks and never went to Cha.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Shun merely submitted a memorial of thanks and never called on Yuan Cha.

manualTranslations.zh: 叉謂順曰：「卿何謂聊不見我？」
manualTranslations.literal: Cha said to Shun, "What do you mean by not once coming to see me?"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yuan Cha said to Shun, "Why have you not come to see me at all?"

manualTranslations.zh: 順正色曰：「天子富於春秋，委政宗輔，叔父宜以至公為心，舉士報國，如何賣恩，責人私謝，豈所望也！」
manualTranslations.literal: Shun said with a stern expression, "The Son of Heaven is young, and government is entrusted to clan assistants. Uncle should take utmost fairness as his heart, promote scholars, and repay the state. How can you sell favors and demand private thanks from people? This is not what one would hope."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Shun answered sternly, "The Son of Heaven is young and has entrusted government to clan ministers. Uncle should act with perfect fairness, raise worthy men, and serve the state. How can you sell favors and demand private thanks? This is not what one expects."

manualTranslations.zh: 至於朝論得失，順常鯁言正議，曾不阿旨，由此見憚。
manualTranslations.literal: As for gains and losses in court discussion, Shun always spoke chokingly direct words and upright arguments, never once flattering the intent; because of this he was feared.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In court debates over right and wrong, Shun always spoke bluntly and argued uprightly, never bending to anyone's wishes; for this he was feared.

manualTranslations.zh: 出除平北將軍、恒州刺史。
manualTranslations.literal: He was sent out and appointed General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Hengzhou.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He was sent out as General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Hengzhou.

manualTranslations.zh: 順謂叉曰：「北鎮紛紜，方為國梗，桑乾舊都，根本所繫，請假都督，為國捍屏。」
manualTranslations.literal: Shun said to Cha, "The northern garrisons are in turmoil and are just now a blockage to the state. Sanggan and the old capital are tied to the root and base. I request temporary authority as commander-in-chief, to serve as shield and screen for the state."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Shun told Yuan Cha, "The northern garrisons are in turmoil and threaten the state. Sanggan and the old capital are bound to our foundation. Give me temporary command, and I will serve as the state's shield."

manualTranslations.zh: 叉心疑難，不欲授以兵官，謂順曰：「此朝廷之事，非我所裁。」
manualTranslations.literal: Cha suspected and found this difficult; not wishing to grant him a military office, he said to Shun, "This is the court's affair, not something I decide."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yuan Cha was suspicious and reluctant to give him a military post, so he said, "This is a court matter, not mine to decide."

manualTranslations.zh: 順曰：「叔父既握國柄，殺生由己，自言天之歷數應在我躬，何得復有朝廷也！」
manualTranslations.literal: Shun said, "Since Uncle holds the handle of the state, killing and giving life come from yourself. You yourself say the heavenly calendar should be in your person; how can there again be a court?"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Shun said, "Uncle holds state power, and life and death come from you. You yourself say Heaven's mandate should rest in your own person; how can there still be a court?"

manualTranslations.zh: 叉彌忿憚之。
manualTranslations.literal: Cha grew still more angry and afraid of him.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yuan Cha grew even angrier and more afraid of him.

manualTranslations.zh: 轉為安東將軍、齊州刺史。
manualTranslations.literal: He was transferred to General Who Pacifies the East and Inspector of Qizhou.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Shun was transferred to General Who Pacifies the East and Inspector of Qizhou.

manualTranslations.zh: 順自負有才，不得居內，每懷鬱怏，形於言色，遂縱酒歡娛，不親政事。
manualTranslations.literal: Shun relied on his own talent, and because he could not remain inside the court, he always harbored resentment, which showed in his words and expression; he then indulged in wine and pleasure and did not attend personally to government affairs.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Confident in his talent and unable to remain at court, Shun nursed resentment that showed in his face and speech. He then gave himself over to wine and amusement and neglected government.

manualTranslations.zh: 叉解領軍，徵為給事黃門侍郎。
manualTranslations.literal: When Cha was relieved of the Guards command, Shun was summoned as Attendant of the Yellow Gate.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Yuan Cha was relieved of command of the Guards, Shun was summoned as Attendant of the Yellow Gate.

manualTranslations.zh: 親友郊迎，賀其得入。
manualTranslations.literal: Relatives and friends met him in the suburbs and congratulated him on being able to enter.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Relatives and friends met him in the suburbs and congratulated him on returning to court.

manualTranslations.zh: 順曰：「不患不入，正恐入而復出耳。」
manualTranslations.literal: Shun said, "I do not worry about not entering; I only fear entering and then going out again."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Shun said, "I am not worried about failing to enter; I only fear entering and then being sent out again."

manualTranslations.zh: 俄兼殿中尚書，轉侍中。
manualTranslations.literal: Soon he concurrently served as Minister of the Palace and was transferred to Palace Attendant.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Soon he concurrently served as Minister of the Palace and was then transferred to Palace Attendant.

manualTranslations.zh: 初，中山王熙起兵討元叉，不果而誅，及靈太后反政，方得改葬。
manualTranslations.literal: Earlier, Xi, Prince of Zhongshan, had raised troops to attack Yuan Cha; he failed and was executed. When Empress Dowager Ling returned to government, only then was he able to be reburied.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Earlier, Xi, Prince of Zhongshan, had raised troops against Yuan Cha, failed, and been executed. Only after Empress Dowager Ling resumed power was he allowed reburial.

manualTranslations.zh: 順侍坐西遊園，因奏太后曰：「臣昨往看中山家葬，非唯宗親哀其冤酷，行路士女，見其一家七喪，皆為澘然，莫不酸泣。」
manualTranslations.literal: Shun was sitting in attendance in the Western Tour Garden and thereupon memorialized to the Empress Dowager, "Yesterday I went to see the burial of Zhongshan's household. Not only did the imperial kin mourn their cruel wrong; men and women on the road, seeing seven funerals from one family, were all moved to tears and sobbed bitterly."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: While sitting in attendance in the Western Tour Garden, Shun said to the Empress Dowager, "Yesterday I went to see the burial of the Zhongshan household. Not only did the imperial kin mourn their cruel wrong; travelers, men and women alike, saw seven dead from one family and all wept bitterly."

manualTranslations.zh: 叉妻時在太后側，順指之曰：「陛下奈何以一妹之故，不伏元叉之罪，使天下懷冤！」
manualTranslations.literal: Cha's wife was then at the Empress Dowager's side. Shun pointed to her and said, "How can Your Majesty, because of one younger sister, not punish Yuan Cha's crime, making all under Heaven harbor injustice?"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yuan Cha's wife was beside the Empress Dowager at the time. Shun pointed to her and said, "How can Your Majesty, for the sake of one sister, fail to punish Yuan Cha's crime and leave the whole realm nursing injustice?"

manualTranslations.zh: 太后默然不語。
manualTranslations.literal: The Empress Dowager was silent and did not speak.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager was silent.

manualTranslations.zh: 就德興反於營州，使尚書盧同往討之，大敗而返。
manualTranslations.literal: Jiu Dexing rebelled in Yingzhou, and the Department official Lu Tong was sent to attack him, but returned in great defeat.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Jiu Dexing rebelled in Yingzhou, Lu Tong of the Department was sent against him but returned after a major defeat.

manualTranslations.zh: 屬侍中穆紹與順侍坐，因論同之罪。
manualTranslations.literal: It happened that Palace Attendant Mu Shao was sitting in attendance with Shun, and they discussed Tong's crime.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Palace Attendant Mu Shao happened to be sitting in attendance with Shun, and they discussed Lu Tong's offense.

manualTranslations.zh: 同先有近宅借紹，紹頗欲為言。
manualTranslations.literal: Tong previously had a nearby residence that he lent to Shao, and Shao rather wished to speak on his behalf.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Lu Tong had earlier lent Shao a nearby residence, and Shao wanted to speak for him.

manualTranslations.zh: 順勃然曰：「盧同終將無罪！」
manualTranslations.literal: Shun suddenly said, "Lu Tong in the end will have no crime!"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Shun suddenly said, "Lu Tong will end up without guilt!"

manualTranslations.zh: 太后曰：「何得如侍中之言？」
manualTranslations.literal: The Empress Dowager said, "How can it be as the Palace Attendant says?"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager said, "How can it be as the Palace Attendant says?"

manualTranslations.zh: 順曰：「同有好宅與要勢侍中，豈慮罪也。」
manualTranslations.literal: Shun said, "Tong has a fine residence to give to an important and powerful Palace Attendant; why would he worry about guilt?"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Shun replied, "Tong has a fine house to give a powerful Palace Attendant. Why should he worry about guilt?"

manualTranslations.zh: 紹慚，不敢復言。
manualTranslations.literal: Shao was ashamed and did not dare speak again.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Shao was ashamed and did not dare speak again.

manualTranslations.zh: 靈太后頗事妝飾，數出遊幸。
manualTranslations.literal: Empress Dowager Ling rather occupied herself with adornment and often went out on pleasure tours.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Ling was much occupied with adornment and often went out on excursions.

manualTranslations.zh: 順面諍曰：「禮，婦人夫喪，自稱未亡人，首去珠玉，衣不被綵。
manualTranslations.literal: Shun remonstrated to her face, saying, "According to ritual, when a woman's husband has died, she calls herself the one not yet dead, removes pearls and jade from her head, and does not wear colored garments.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Shun remonstrated with her directly: "According to ritual, when a woman loses her husband she calls herself the one not yet dead, removes pearls and jade from her hair, and does not wear colored clothing.

manualTranslations.zh: 陛下母臨天下，年垂不惑，過甚修飾，何以示後世？」
manualTranslations.literal: Your Majesty mothers all under Heaven and is nearly forty, yet you excessively cultivate adornment. How will you show yourself to later generations?"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Your Majesty rules the realm as mother and is nearly forty, yet you adorn yourself excessively. What example does this show later generations?"

manualTranslations.zh: 靈太后慚而不出。
manualTranslations.literal: Empress Dowager Ling was ashamed and did not go out.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Ling was ashamed and stopped going out.

manualTranslations.zh: 還入宮，責順曰：「千里相徵，豈欲眾中見辱也！」
manualTranslations.literal: After returning to the palace, she reproached Shun, saying, "I summoned you from a thousand li away; did I mean to be humiliated before the crowd?"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When she returned to the palace, she rebuked Shun: "I summoned you from a thousand li away; did you intend to shame me in public?"

manualTranslations.zh: 順曰：「陛下盛服炫容，不畏天下所笑，何耻臣之一言乎？」
manualTranslations.literal: Shun said, "Your Majesty wears splendid robes and dazzles with your appearance, yet does not fear the laughter of all under Heaven. Why be ashamed of one word from me?"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Shun replied, "Your Majesty dresses splendidly and displays your beauty without fearing the laughter of the realm. Why be ashamed of one word from me?"

manualTranslations.zh: 初，城陽王徽慕順才名，偏相結納。
manualTranslations.literal: Earlier, Hui, Prince of Chengyang, admired Shun's talent and reputation and especially befriended and received him.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Earlier, Hui, Prince of Chengyang, admired Shun's talent and reputation and made special efforts to befriend him.

manualTranslations.zh: 而廣陽王淵姦徽妻于氏，大為嫌隙。
manualTranslations.literal: But Yuan, Prince of Guangyang, committed adultery with Hui's wife, Lady Yu, creating a great rift.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: But Yuan, Prince of Guangyang, had an affair with Hui's wife Lady Yu, creating a deep rift.

manualTranslations.zh: 及淵自定州被徵，入為吏部尚書，兼中領軍。
manualTranslations.literal: When Yuan was summoned from Dingzhou and entered as Minister of Personnel, concurrently Central Commander of the Guards,
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Yuan was summoned from Dingzhou to serve as Minister of Personnel and concurrently Central Commander of the Guards,

manualTranslations.zh: 順為詔書，辭頗優美。
manualTranslations.literal: Shun drafted the edict for him, and its wording was quite excellent.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Shun drafted the edict for him in notably elegant language.

manualTranslations.zh: 徽疑順為淵左右，由是與徐紇間順於靈太后，出順為護軍將軍、太常卿。
manualTranslations.literal: Hui suspected Shun of siding with Yuan, and because of this, together with Xu He, he alienated Shun from Empress Dowager Ling; Shun was sent out as General Who Protects the Army and Chamberlain for Ceremonials.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Hui suspected Shun of favoring Yuan, so he and Xu He slandered Shun to Empress Dowager Ling. Shun was sent out as General Who Protects the Army and Chamberlain for Ceremonials.

manualTranslations.zh: 順奉辭於西遊園，徽紇侍側，順指之謂靈太后曰：「此人魏之宰嚭，魏國不滅，終不死亡。」
manualTranslations.literal: Shun took leave in the Western Tour Garden, with Hui and He standing in attendance at the side. Shun pointed to them and said to Empress Dowager Ling, "This man is Wei's Zai Pi; if the state of Wei is not destroyed, he will never die."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Shun took leave in the Western Tour Garden while Hui and Xu He stood at the side. Pointing at Xu He, he said to Empress Dowager Ling, "This man is Wei's Zai Pi. Unless Wei is destroyed, he will never die."

manualTranslations.zh: 紇脅肩而出。
manualTranslations.literal: He went out with his shoulders hunched.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Xu He went out with his shoulders hunched.

manualTranslations.zh: 順遂抗聲叱之曰：「爾刀筆小人，正堪為几案之吏，寧應忝茲執戟，虧我彝倫！」
manualTranslations.literal: Shun then raised his voice and rebuked him, saying, "You petty knife-and-brush man are fit only to be a desk clerk. How could you shamefully hold this halberd and damage our proper human relations!"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Shun then shouted after him, "You petty clerk with knife and brush are fit only for desk work. How can you presume to hold a halberd here and disgrace our proper order!"

manualTranslations.zh: 遂振衣而起。
manualTranslations.literal: He then shook out his robe and rose.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He shook out his robe and rose.

manualTranslations.zh: 靈太后默而不言。
manualTranslations.literal: Empress Dowager Ling was silent and did not speak.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Ling said nothing.

manualTranslations.zh: 時追論順父顧託之功，增任城王彝邑二千戶，又析彝邑五百戶以封順，為東阿縣開國公。
manualTranslations.literal: At the time the court was retrospectively discussing the merit of Shun's father in receiving the testamentary charge. It increased the fief of Yi, Prince of Rencheng, by two thousand households, and also divided five hundred households from Yi's fief to enfeoff Shun as Founding Duke of Dong'e County.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: At the time the court was reviewing the merit of Shun's father in the imperial entrustment. Yi, Prince of Rencheng, received two thousand additional households, and five hundred households were carved from Yi's fief to enfeoff Shun as Founding Duke of Dong'e County.

manualTranslations.zh: 順疾徽等間之，遂為蠅賦曰：「余以仲秋休沐，端坐衡門，寄想琴書，託情紙翰，而蒼蠅小蟲，往來牀几，疾其變白，聊為賦云：遐哉大道，廓矣洪氛。
manualTranslations.literal: Shun hated that Hui and the others had alienated him, and so he composed a Rhapsody on Flies, saying, "In mid-autumn, while resting from office, I sat upright by my humble gate, setting my thoughts on zither and books and entrusting my feelings to paper and brush; but the small insects, the bluebottle flies, came and went over bed and table. Hating how they change white, I have briefly made a rhapsody, saying: Vast is the great Way, broad the primal vapor.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Shun hated Hui and the others for slandering him, and so he wrote a Rhapsody on Flies: "In mid-autumn, resting from office, I sat quietly at my humble gate, my thoughts on zither and books and my feelings entrusted to paper and brush. But tiny bluebottle flies came and went over bed and table. Hating how they transform white, I have made this rhapsody: Vast is the great Way, broad the primal vapor.

manualTranslations.zh: 肇立秋夏，爰啟冬春。
manualTranslations.literal: It first established autumn and summer, and then opened winter and spring.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: It first set autumn and summer in place, then opened winter and spring.

manualTranslations.zh: 既含育於萬性，又芻狗而不仁。
manualTranslations.literal: It both contains and nurtures the ten thousand natures, and yet, like straw dogs, is not benevolent.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: It contains and nurtures all natures, yet like straw dogs it is not benevolent.

manualTranslations.zh: 隨因緣以授體，齊美惡而無分。
manualTranslations.literal: Following causes and conditions, it grants bodies, equalizing beautiful and ugly without distinction.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Following conditions, it grants bodies, making no distinction between fair and foul.

manualTranslations.zh: 生茲穢類，靡益於人。
manualTranslations.literal: It gives birth to this filthy kind, with no benefit to human beings.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Thus this filthy kind is born, bringing no benefit to people.

manualTranslations.zh: 名備羣品，聲損眾倫。
manualTranslations.literal: Its name is included among the many creatures, but its sound damages all relations.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Its name is counted among living things, but its buzzing harms the order of all beings.

manualTranslations.zh: 欹脛纖翼，紫首蒼身。
manualTranslations.literal: Crooked shins and slender wings, purple heads and blue bodies.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Crooked legs, slender wings, purple heads, blue bodies.

manualTranslations.zh: 飛不能迥，聲若遠聞。
manualTranslations.literal: It cannot fly far, but its sound seems heard from afar.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: It cannot fly far, yet its noise seems to carry into the distance.

manualTranslations.zh: 點緇成素，變白為黑。
manualTranslations.literal: It dots black and makes white; it changes white into black.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: It spots black onto white and turns white into black.

manualTranslations.zh: 寡愛蘭芳，偏貪穢食。
manualTranslations.literal: It has little love for orchid fragrance and is especially greedy for filthy food.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: It cares little for orchid fragrance and craves filthy food.

manualTranslations.zh: 集桓公之屍，居平叔之側。
manualTranslations.literal: It gathered on Duke Huan's corpse and dwelt by Pingshu's side.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: It gathered on Duke Huan's corpse and lingered at Pingshu's side.

manualTranslations.zh: 亂鷄鳴之響，毀皇宮之飾。
manualTranslations.literal: It disordered the sound of the cockcrow and ruined the ornaments of the imperial palace.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: It confused the sound of the cockcrow and defiled the ornaments of the imperial palace.

manualTranslations.zh: 習習戶庭，營營榛棘。
manualTranslations.literal: Fluttering through doors and courtyards, buzzing among thorns and brambles.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Fluttering through doors and courtyards, buzzing among thorns and brambles.

manualTranslations.zh: 反覆往還，譬彼讒賊。
manualTranslations.literal: Back and forth it goes and returns, like those slanderous rebels.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Back and forth it comes and goes, like slanderous traitors.

manualTranslations.zh: 膚受既通，譖潤罔極。
manualTranslations.literal: Once skin-deep slander gets through, soaking accusations have no limit.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Once slander penetrates the skin, its soaking accusations know no limit.

manualTranslations.zh: 緝緝幡幡，交亂四國。
manualTranslations.literal: Whispering and fluttering, they cross and disorder the four states.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Whispering and fluttering, they throw the four quarters into disorder.

manualTranslations.zh: 於是妖姬進，邪士來，聖賢擁，忠孝摧。
manualTranslations.literal: Thereupon seductive women advance, wicked men come, sages and worthies are blocked, and the loyal and filial are crushed.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Then seductive women advance, wicked men arrive, sages and worthies are blocked, and the loyal and filial are crushed.

manualTranslations.zh: 周昌拘於牖里，天乙囚於夏臺。
manualTranslations.literal: Zhou Chang was confined at Youli, and Tianyi was imprisoned at Xiatai.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Zhou Chang was confined at Youli, and Tianyi imprisoned at Xiatai.

manualTranslations.zh: 伯奇為之痛結，申生為之蒙災。
manualTranslations.literal: Boqi was knotted in pain by them, and Shensheng was covered with disaster by them.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Boqi was bound in grief because of them, and Shensheng was overtaken by disaster because of them.

manualTranslations.zh: 鴟鴞悲其室，採葛懼其懷。
manualTranslations.literal: The Owl grieved for its house, and Gathering Kudzu feared what was in the heart.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Owl lamented its ruined house, and Gathering Kudzu feared what lay in the heart.

manualTranslations.zh: 小弁隕其涕，靈均表其哀。
manualTranslations.literal: Xiaobian shed its tears, and Lingjun displayed his sorrow.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Xiaobian shed tears, and Lingjun made his sorrow known.

manualTranslations.zh: 自古明哲猶如此，何況中庸與凡才。
manualTranslations.literal: From antiquity, the enlightened and wise were still like this; how much more the middling and ordinary talents?
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Even the enlightened and wise of antiquity suffered so; how much more men of middling or ordinary talent?

manualTranslations.zh: 若夫天生地養，各有所親。
manualTranslations.literal: As for what Heaven gives birth to and Earth nourishes, each has what it is close to.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: As for the beings Heaven gives birth to and Earth nourishes, each has its proper affinities.

manualTranslations.zh: 獸必依地，鳥亦憑雲。
manualTranslations.literal: Beasts must rely on the earth, and birds also depend on the clouds.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Beasts rely on the earth, and birds depend on the clouds.

manualTranslations.zh: 或來儀以呈祉，或自擾而見文。
manualTranslations.literal: Some come in ritual display to present blessings; some are tamed and show patterned beauty.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Some come in stately display to present blessings; some are domesticated and display patterned beauty.

manualTranslations.zh: 或負圖而歸德，或銜書以告真。
manualTranslations.literal: Some bear diagrams and return to virtue; some hold writings in their mouths and announce the true.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Some bear diagrams and return to virtue; some carry writings in their mouths to reveal the true.

manualTranslations.zh: 或夭胎而奉味，或殘軀以獻珍。
manualTranslations.literal: Some are cut short in the womb to offer flavor; some offer preciousness with damaged bodies.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Some are taken before birth to provide flavor; some, with damaged bodies, offer delicacies.

manualTranslations.zh: 或主皮而興禮，或牢豢以供神。
manualTranslations.literal: Some, as hides, promote ritual; some, as stall-fed animals, supply the spirits.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Some, as hides, give rise to ritual; some, as sacrificial animals, serve the spirits.

manualTranslations.zh: 雖死生之異質，俱有益於國人。
manualTranslations.literal: Although dead and living are different in substance, all are of benefit to the people of the state.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Though they differ as living and dead, all benefit the people of the state.

manualTranslations.zh: 非如蒼蠅之無用，唯構亂於蒸民。」
manualTranslations.literal: They are not like the bluebottle fly, which is useless and only constructs disorder among the multitudes."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: They are not like the bluebottle fly, useless and only sowing disorder among the people."

manualTranslations.zh: 遂屬疾在家，杜絕慶弔。
manualTranslations.literal: He then became ill at home and cut off congratulations and condolences.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He then fell ill at home and refused all visits of congratulation or condolence.

manualTranslations.zh: 後除吏部尚書，兼右僕射。
manualTranslations.literal: Later he was appointed Minister of Personnel and concurrently Right Vice Director.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Later he was appointed Minister of Personnel and concurrently Right Vice Director.

manualTranslations.zh: 及上省，登階向榻，見榻甚故，問都令史徐仵起。
manualTranslations.literal: When he went up to the Department, climbed the steps toward the couch, and saw that the couch was very old, he asked the Chief Clerk Xu Wuqi about it.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When he went up to the Department and approached the couch, he saw that it was very old and asked Chief Clerk Xu Wuqi about it.

manualTranslations.zh: 仵起曰：「此榻曾經先王坐。」
manualTranslations.literal: Wuqi said, "This couch was once sat on by the former king."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Wuqi said, "The former prince once sat on this couch."

manualTranslations.zh: 順即哽塞，涕泗交流，久而不能言，遂令換之。
manualTranslations.literal: Shun immediately choked up, tears and mucus flowing together; for a long while he could not speak, and he then ordered it changed.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Shun immediately choked up, tears streaming down; for a long while he could not speak, and then ordered the couch replaced.

manualTranslations.zh: 時三公曹令史朱暉，素事錄尚書、高陽王雍，雍欲以為廷尉評，頻請託順，順不為用。
manualTranslations.literal: At the time Zhu Hui, a clerk in the Bureau of the Three Excellencies, had long served Yong, Recording Director of the Department and Prince of Gaoyang. Yong wished to make him an Evaluator in the Court of Justice and repeatedly asked and entrusted Shun, but Shun would not employ him.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: At the time Zhu Hui, a clerk in the Bureau of the Three Excellencies, had long served Yuan Yong, Prince of Gaoyang and Recording Director of the Department. Yong wanted to make him an Evaluator in the Court of Justice and repeatedly pressed Shun, but Shun refused to use him.

manualTranslations.zh: 雍遂下命用之，順投之於地。
manualTranslations.literal: Yong then issued an order to use him, and Shun threw it on the ground.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yuan Yong then issued an order appointing him, and Shun threw it on the ground.

manualTranslations.zh: 雍聞之，大怒，昧爽坐都廳，召尚書及丞郎畢集，欲待順至，於眾挫之。
manualTranslations.literal: When Yong heard of this, he was furious. At dawn he sat in the metropolitan hall and summoned the Ministers, Aides, and Gentlemen to assemble completely, intending to wait for Shun to arrive and humiliate him before the crowd.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Yong heard, he was furious. At dawn he sat in the metropolitan hall and summoned all the Ministers, Aides, and Gentlemen, intending to humiliate Shun publicly when he arrived.

manualTranslations.zh: 順日高方至，雍攘袂撫几而言曰：「身，天子之子，天子之弟，天子之叔，天子之相，四海之內，親尊莫二，元順何人，以身成命，投棄於地！」
manualTranslations.literal: Only when the sun was high did Shun arrive. Yong rolled up his sleeves, struck the armrest, and said, "I am son of the Son of Heaven, brother of the Son of Heaven, uncle of the Son of Heaven, and minister of the Son of Heaven. Within the four seas none is closer or more honored. What sort of man is Yuan Shun, to take an order completed by me and throw it away on the ground!"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Shun arrived only when the sun was high. Yong rolled up his sleeves, struck the table, and said, "I am the Son of Heaven's son, brother, uncle, and chief minister. Within the four seas no one is closer or more honored. Who is Yuan Shun, to take my completed order and throw it on the ground!"

manualTranslations.zh: 順鬚鬢俱張，仰面看屋，憤氣奔涌，長歔而不言。
manualTranslations.literal: Shun's beard and temples both bristled; he raised his face and looked at the roof, angry breath surging, and sighed long without speaking.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Shun's beard and temples bristled. He looked up at the rafters, anger surging, and gave a long sigh without speaking.

manualTranslations.zh: 久之，搖一白羽扇，徐而謂雍曰：「高祖遷宅中土，創定九流，官方清濁，軌儀萬古。
manualTranslations.literal: After a long while, he waved a white feather fan and slowly said to Yong, "Gaozu moved his residence to the central lands and first fixed the nine ranks; offices were divided into pure and impure, a model for ten thousand ages.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: After a long while, he waved a white feather fan and slowly said to Yong, "Gaozu moved the capital to the central lands and established the nine ranks; he distinguished pure and impure offices, setting a model for all ages.

manualTranslations.zh: 而朱暉小子，身為省吏，何合為廷尉清官！
manualTranslations.literal: Yet Zhu Hui is a petty man, himself a department clerk. How is he fit for a pure office in the Court of Justice?
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Zhu Hui is a petty man, a mere Department clerk. How is he fit for a pure office in the Court of Justice?

manualTranslations.zh: 殿下既先皇同氣，宜遵成旨，自有短垣而復踰之也。」
manualTranslations.literal: Since Your Highness is of the same breath as the former emperor, you should follow the completed decree. There is already a low wall, and yet you overstep it again."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Your Highness shares the late emperor's blood and should follow the established decree. Even a low wall is still a boundary; why overstep it again?"

manualTranslations.zh: 雍曰：「身為丞相、錄尚書，如何不得用一人為官？」
manualTranslations.literal: Yong said, "I am Chancellor and Recording Director of the Department of State Affairs; how can I not be allowed to use one man as an official?"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yong said, "I am Chancellor and Recording Director of the Department. How can I not appoint one man to office?"

manualTranslations.zh: 順曰：「庖人雖不治庖，尸祝不得越樽俎而代之。
manualTranslations.literal: Shun said, "Though the cook does not manage the kitchen, the invocator may not step past the wine vessels and stands to replace him.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Shun replied, "Even if the cook does not manage the kitchen, the invocator may not step beyond the vessels and stands to take his place.

manualTranslations.zh: 未聞有別旨，令殿下參選事。」
manualTranslations.literal: I have not heard of a separate decree ordering Your Highness to take part in selection affairs."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: I have heard of no separate edict ordering Your Highness to take part in personnel selection."

manualTranslations.zh: 順又厲聲曰：「殿下必如是，順當依事奏聞！」
manualTranslations.literal: Shun again said in a stern voice, "If Your Highness insists on being like this, I shall memorialize the matter according to the facts!"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Shun then said sharply, "If Your Highness insists, I will memorialize the matter according to the facts!"

manualTranslations.zh: 雍遂笑而言曰：「豈可以朱暉小人，便相忿恨。」
manualTranslations.literal: Yong then laughed and said, "How could we become angry with each other over a petty man like Zhu Hui?"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yong then laughed. "How could we become angry with one another over a petty man like Zhu Hui?"

manualTranslations.zh: 遂起，呼順入室，與之極飲。
manualTranslations.literal: He then rose, called Shun into the inner room, and drank with him to the utmost.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He rose, called Shun inside, and drank with him to the fullest.

manualTranslations.zh: 順之亢毅不撓，皆此類也。
manualTranslations.literal: Shun's lofty firmness and refusal to bend were all of this kind.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Shun's lofty firmness and refusal to bend were all of this sort.

manualTranslations.zh: 後除征南將軍、右光祿大夫，轉兼左僕射。
manualTranslations.literal: Later he was appointed General Who Conquers the South and Right Guanglu Grandee, and was transferred to concurrently serve as Left Vice Director.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Later he was appointed General Who Conquers the South and Right Guanglu Grandee, then transferred to concurrently serve as Left Vice Director.

manualTranslations.zh: 爾朱榮之奉莊帝，召百官悉至河陰，素聞順數諫諍，惜其亮直，謂朱瑞曰：「可語元僕射，但在省，不須來。」
manualTranslations.literal: When Erzhu Rong received Emperor Zhuang, he summoned all the officials to Heyin. He had long heard that Shun had repeatedly remonstrated and argued, and he cherished his bright uprightness, so he said to Zhu Rui, "You may tell Vice Director Yuan only to remain in the Department; he need not come."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Erzhu Rong received Emperor Zhuang, he summoned all officials to Heyin. Having long heard that Shun often remonstrated and valuing his clear integrity, he told Zhu Rui, "Tell Vice Director Yuan to stay in the Department; he need not come."

manualTranslations.zh: 順不達其旨，聞害衣冠，遂便出走，為陵戶鮮于康奴所害。
manualTranslations.literal: Shun did not understand his intent. Hearing that the officials were being harmed, he immediately fled and was killed by Xianyu Kangnu, a tomb household man.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Shun did not understand the warning. Hearing that the officials were being slaughtered, he fled and was killed by Xianyu Kangnu, a tomb-household man.

manualTranslations.zh: 家徒四壁，無物斂屍，止有書數千卷而已。
manualTranslations.literal: His house had only four bare walls, and there was nothing with which to enshroud the corpse; there were only several thousand scrolls of books.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: His house was bare, with nothing to shroud his body; it contained only several thousand scrolls of books.

manualTranslations.zh: 門下通事令史王才達裂裳覆之。
manualTranslations.literal: Wang Caida, Clerk for Communications under the Gate, tore his garment to cover him.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Wang Caida, Clerk for Communications under the Gate, tore his robe to cover the body.

manualTranslations.zh: 莊帝還宮，遣黃門侍郎山偉巡喻京邑。
manualTranslations.literal: When Emperor Zhuang returned to the palace, he sent Yellow Gate Attendant Shan Wei to tour and reassure the capital.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhuang returned to the palace, he sent Yellow Gate Attendant Shan Wei to tour the capital and reassure it.

manualTranslations.zh: 偉臨順喪，悲慟無已。
manualTranslations.literal: Wei came to Shun's funeral and grieved without cease.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Shan Wei visited Shun's mourning place and wept without stopping.

manualTranslations.zh: 既還，莊帝怪而問曰：「黃門何為聲散？」
manualTranslations.literal: After he returned, Emperor Zhuang was surprised and asked, "Why is the Yellow Gate's voice broken?"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When he returned, Emperor Zhuang was surprised and asked, "Why is the Yellow Gate attendant's voice hoarse?"

manualTranslations.zh: 偉以狀對。
manualTranslations.literal: Wei answered with the circumstances.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Shan Wei told him what had happened.

manualTranslations.zh: 莊帝敕侍中元祉曰：「宗室喪亡非一，不可周贍。
manualTranslations.literal: Emperor Zhuang ordered Palace Attendant Yuan Zhi, "There is more than one death in the imperial clan, and they cannot all be fully provided for.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhuang instructed Palace Attendant Yuan Zhi, "Many members of the imperial clan have died, and we cannot provide fully for all of them.

manualTranslations.zh: 元僕射清苦之節，死乃益彰，特贈絹百匹，餘不得例。」
manualTranslations.literal: The austere integrity of Vice Director Yuan is only more manifest in death. Specially grant him one hundred bolts of silk; the rest may not follow this as precedent."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Vice Director Yuan's austere integrity shines even more in death. Grant him one hundred bolts of silk as a special gift; let this not become precedent for the others."

manualTranslations.zh: 贈驃騎大將軍、尚書令、司徒公、定州刺史，諡曰文烈。
manualTranslations.literal: He was posthumously granted Grand General of Agile Cavalry, Director of the Department of State Affairs, Minister over the Masses, and Inspector of Dingzhou, with the posthumous title Wenlie.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted Grand General of Agile Cavalry, Director of the Department of State Affairs, Minister over the Masses, and Inspector of Dingzhou, and was given the posthumous title Wenlie.

manualTranslations.zh: 順撰帝錄二十卷，詩賦表頌數十篇，今多亡失。
manualTranslations.literal: Shun compiled Imperial Records in twenty fascicles, as well as several tens of poems, rhapsodies, memorials, and eulogies; most are now lost.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Shun compiled Imperial Records in twenty fascicles and wrote several dozen poems, rhapsodies, memorials, and eulogies, most of which are now lost.

manualTranslations.zh: 長子朗，時年十七。
manualTranslations.literal: His eldest son Lang was seventeen at the time.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: His eldest son Lang was seventeen at the time.

manualTranslations.zh: 枕戈潛伏積年，乃手刃康奴，以首祭於順墓，然後詣闕請罪。
manualTranslations.literal: He slept on his spear and hid in secret for years, then personally killed Kangnu, sacrificed the head at Shun's tomb, and only afterward went to the palace gate to confess his crime.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: For years he slept on his spear and hid in secret. Then he killed Kangnu with his own hand, offered the head at Shun's tomb, and afterward went to the palace gate to confess.

manualTranslations.zh: 朝廷嘉而不問。
manualTranslations.literal: The court praised him and did not prosecute.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The court praised him and did not punish him.

manualTranslations.zh: 朗涉歷書記，為司徒屬。
manualTranslations.literal: Lang had experience in documents and records and served as an attendant to the Minister over the Masses.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Lang was experienced in documents and records and served as an attendant to the Minister over the Masses.

manualTranslations.zh: 天平中，為奴所害。
manualTranslations.literal: In the Tianping era, he was killed by a slave.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the Tianping era, he was killed by a slave.

manualTranslations.zh: 贈都督瀛冀二州諸軍事、□□將軍、尚書右僕射、冀州刺史。
manualTranslations.literal: He was posthumously granted Commander of all military affairs in Ying and Ji provinces, General with title missing, Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, and Inspector of Jizhou.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted Commander of all military affairs in Ying and Ji provinces, an unspecified generalship, Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, and Inspector of Jizhou.

manualTranslations.zh: 順弟淑，淑弟悲，並早卒。
manualTranslations.literal: Shun's younger brother Shu and Shu's younger brother Bei both died young.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Shun's younger brother Shu and Shu's younger brother Bei both died young.

manualTranslations.zh: 悲弟紀，字子綱。
manualTranslations.literal: Bei's younger brother Ji was styled Zigang.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Bei's younger brother Ji was styled Zigang.

manualTranslations.zh: 永熙中，給事黃門侍郎。
manualTranslations.literal: In the Yongxi era, he was Attendant of the Yellow Gate.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the Yongxi era he served as Attendant of the Yellow Gate.

manualTranslations.zh: 隨出帝，沒於關中。
manualTranslations.literal: He followed the Emperor Who Went Out and died in Guanzhong.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He followed the Emperor Who Went Out and died in Guanzhong.

manualTranslations.zh: 澄弟嵩，字道岳。
manualTranslations.literal: Cheng's younger brother Song was styled Daoyue.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Cheng's younger brother Song was styled Daoyue.

manualTranslations.zh: 高祖時，自中大夫遷員外常侍，轉步兵校尉。
manualTranslations.literal: In Gaozu's time, he was transferred from Palace Grandee to Regular Attendant Outside the Ranks, then transferred to Infantry Commandant.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In Gaozu's time he moved from Palace Grandee to Regular Attendant Outside the Ranks, then became Infantry Commandant.

manualTranslations.zh: 大司馬、安定王休薨，未及卒哭，嵩便遊田。
manualTranslations.literal: When Xiu, Grand Marshal and Prince of Anding, died, before the final wailing had been completed, Song immediately went hunting.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Xiu, Grand Marshal and Prince of Anding, died, Song went hunting before the mourning rites had even ended.

manualTranslations.zh: 高祖聞而大怒，詔曰：「嵩不能克己復禮，企心典憲，大司馬薨殂甫爾，便以鷹鷂自娛。
manualTranslations.literal: When Gaozu heard of this, he was furious and issued an edict: "Song cannot overcome himself and return to ritual or set his mind on standards and laws. The Grand Marshal has only just died, and he immediately amuses himself with hawks and sparrowhawks.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Gaozu heard, he was furious and issued an edict: "Song cannot master himself and return to ritual or set his mind on law and precedent. The Grand Marshal has only just died, and already he amuses himself with hawks and falcons.

manualTranslations.zh: 有如父之痛，無猶子之情，捐心棄禮，何其太速！
manualTranslations.literal: He has pain as though for a father, but lacks the feeling of a nephew; he casts aside feeling and abandons ritual. How far too quick this is!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He should feel pain as for a father, yet he lacks even a nephew's feeling; he casts aside feeling and abandons ritual. How terribly hasty!

manualTranslations.zh: 便可免官。」
manualTranslations.literal: He may be dismissed from office."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He may be dismissed from office."

manualTranslations.zh: 後從平沔北，累有戰功，除左中郎將，兼武衞將軍。
manualTranslations.literal: Later he followed in pacifying north of the Mian, repeatedly had battle merits, and was appointed Left Gentleman General of the Center, concurrently General of the Martial Guard.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Later he took part in pacifying the north of the Mian, repeatedly earned battle merit, and was appointed Left Gentleman General of the Center, concurrently General of the Martial Guard.

manualTranslations.zh: 高祖南伐，蕭寶卷將陳顯達率眾拒戰。
manualTranslations.literal: When Gaozu campaigned south, Xiao Baojuan's general Chen Xianda led troops to resist in battle.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Gaozu campaigned south, Xiao Baojuan's general Chen Xianda led troops to resist him.

manualTranslations.zh: 嵩身備三仗，免冑直前，將士從之，顯達奔潰，斬獲萬計。
manualTranslations.literal: Song himself was equipped with three weapons, removed his helmet, and advanced straight ahead. The officers and soldiers followed him, Xianda fled in collapse, and beheadings and captures were counted by the ten thousand.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Song armed himself with three weapons, removed his helmet, and advanced straight ahead. The officers and soldiers followed; Xianda's forces fled in collapse, and the dead and captured numbered in the tens of thousands.

manualTranslations.zh: 嵩於爾日勇冠三軍。
manualTranslations.literal: On that day Song's courage topped the three armies.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: That day, Song's courage surpassed the whole army.

manualTranslations.zh: 高祖大悅而言曰：「任城康王大有褔德，文武頓出其門。」
manualTranslations.literal: Gaozu was greatly pleased and said, "Prince Kang of Rencheng has great fortune and virtue; civil and martial talent have suddenly emerged from his gate."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Gaozu was delighted. "Prince Kang of Rencheng had great fortune and virtue; civil and martial talent have both burst from his household."

manualTranslations.zh: 以功賜爵高平縣侯，賚帛二千五百匹。
manualTranslations.literal: For his merit he was granted the title Marquis of Gaoping County and given two thousand five hundred bolts of silk.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: For his merit he was granted the title Marquis of Gaoping County and awarded twenty-five hundred bolts of silk.

manualTranslations.zh: 初，高祖之發洛也，馮皇后以罪幽於宮內。
manualTranslations.literal: Earlier, when Gaozu departed Luoyang, Empress Feng had been confined inside the palace for an offense.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Gaozu left Luoyang, Empress Feng had been confined inside the palace for an offense.

manualTranslations.zh: 既平顯達，回次穀唐原，高祖疾甚，將賜后死，曰：「使人不易可得。」
manualTranslations.literal: After Xianda had been pacified, on the return they stopped at Gutangyuan. Gaozu was gravely ill and was about to grant the empress death, saying, "A suitable envoy is not easy to obtain."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: After Xianda was defeated, Gaozu stopped on the return at Gutangyuan. Gravely ill, he was about to order the empress to die and said, "A suitable envoy is not easy to find."

manualTranslations.zh: 顧謂任城王澄曰：「任城必不負我，嵩亦當不負任城，可使嵩也。」
manualTranslations.literal: He looked back and said to Cheng, Prince of Rencheng, "Rencheng will surely not fail me, and Song will also not fail Rencheng. Song may be sent."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He turned to Cheng, Prince of Rencheng: "Rencheng will not fail me, and Song will not fail Rencheng. Send Song."

manualTranslations.zh: 於是引嵩入內，親詔遣之。
manualTranslations.literal: Thereupon Song was brought inside, and Gaozu personally issued an edict dispatching him.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Song was then brought inside, and Gaozu personally ordered him dispatched.

manualTranslations.zh: 世宗即位，以武衞將軍兼侍中，出為平南將軍、荊州刺史。
manualTranslations.literal: When Shizong took the throne, Song served as General of the Martial Guard concurrently Palace Attendant, and was sent out as General Who Pacifies the South and Inspector of Jingzhou.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Shizong ascended the throne, Song served as General of the Martial Guard and concurrently Palace Attendant, then was sent out as General Who Pacifies the South and Inspector of Jingzhou.

manualTranslations.zh: 嵩表曰：「蕭寶卷骨肉相殘，忠良先戮，臣下囂然，莫不離背，君臣攜貳，干戈日尋。
manualTranslations.literal: Song memorialized, "Xiao Baojuan's own flesh and blood harm one another, loyal and good men are first killed, his ministers are in uproar, and none fails to leave and turn away. Ruler and ministers are divided, and weapons are sought daily.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Song memorialized, "Xiao Baojuan slaughters his own kin and kills loyal men first. His ministers are in uproar and all are turning from him. Ruler and ministers are divided, and war grows daily.

manualTranslations.zh: 流聞寶卷雍州刺史蕭衍兄懿於建業阻兵，與寶卷相持，荊郢二州刺史並是寶卷之弟，必有圖衍之志。
manualTranslations.literal: I have heard it said that Xiao Yi, elder brother of Baojuan's Inspector of Yongzhou Xiao Yan, is holding troops at Jianye and opposing Baojuan, while the Inspectors of Jingzhou and Yingzhou are both Baojuan's younger brothers and surely intend to scheme against Yan.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: I have heard that Xiao Yi, elder brother of Xiao Yan, Baojuan's Inspector of Yongzhou, is holding troops at Jianye against Baojuan; the Inspectors of Jingzhou and Yingzhou are both Baojuan's younger brothers and surely plan to move against Yan.

manualTranslations.zh: 臣若遣書相聞，迎其本謀，冀獲同心，并力除衍。
manualTranslations.literal: If I send letters to communicate with them and meet their original plan, I hope to obtain common purpose and combine strength to eliminate Yan.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: If I send letters and meet them in their own plans, we may act with one mind and combine forces to eliminate Yan.

manualTranslations.zh: 平衍之後，彼必旋師赴救丹陽，當不能復經營疆陲，全固襄沔。
manualTranslations.literal: After Yan is pacified, they will surely turn their armies back to rescue Danyang, and then will no longer be able to manage the frontier and fully secure Xiang and Mian.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Once Yan is pacified, they will have to turn back to rescue Danyang and will no longer be able to manage the frontier or secure Xiang and Mian.

manualTranslations.zh: 臣之軍威已得臨據，則沔南之地可一舉而收。
manualTranslations.literal: If my army's power has already reached and occupied a commanding position, then the land south of the Mian can be taken in one move.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: If our army has already established a commanding position, the land south of the Mian can be taken in a single move.

manualTranslations.zh: 緣漢曜兵，示以威德，思歸有道者則引而納之，受疑告危者則援而接之。
manualTranslations.literal: By displaying troops along the Han and showing them awe and virtue, those who think of returning to the Way can be drawn in and received, and those who are under suspicion and report danger can be aided and accepted.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: If we display troops along the Han and show both power and virtue, those who wish to return to the Way can be welcomed, and those in danger under suspicion can be rescued and received.

manualTranslations.zh: 總兵竚銳，觀釁伺隙，若其零落之形已彰，怠懈之勢已著，便可順流摧鋒，長驅席卷。」
manualTranslations.literal: With the army gathered and its edge held ready, we can observe rifts and wait for openings. If their form of collapse is already clear and their slackened condition already manifest, then we can follow the current, crush their front, drive deep, and roll them up like a mat."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: With troops gathered and ready, we can watch for cracks and openings. Once their collapse is clear and their slackness plain, we can move with the current, break their front, drive deep, and sweep them up like a mat."

manualTranslations.zh: 詔曰：「所陳嘉謀，深是良計。
manualTranslations.literal: The edict said, "The excellent plan you set forth is deeply a good strategy.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The edict said, "The fine plan you present is truly sound strategy.

manualTranslations.zh: 如當機形可進，任將軍裁之。」
manualTranslations.literal: If the opportunity and situation allow advance, it is entrusted to the General to decide."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: If the moment and situation permit an advance, the General may decide."

manualTranslations.zh: 既而蕭衍尋克建業，乃止。
manualTranslations.literal: Soon afterward Xiao Yan captured Jianye, and so the matter stopped.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Xiao Yan captured Jianye, and the plan was dropped.

manualTranslations.zh: 除平北將軍、恒州刺史。
manualTranslations.literal: He was appointed General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Hengzhou.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Song was appointed General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Hengzhou.

manualTranslations.zh: 轉平東將軍、徐州刺史。
manualTranslations.literal: He was transferred to General Who Pacifies the East and Inspector of Xuzhou.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He was transferred to General Who Pacifies the East and Inspector of Xuzhou.

manualTranslations.zh: 又轉安南將軍、揚州刺史。
manualTranslations.literal: He was again transferred to General Who Pacifies the South and Inspector of Yangzhou.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He was later transferred again as General Who Pacifies the South and Inspector of Yangzhou.

manualTranslations.zh: 蕭衍湘州刺史楊公則率眾二萬，屯軍洛口，姜慶真領卒五千，據於首陂，又遣其左軍將軍騫小眼，軍主何天祚、張俊興等率眾七千，攻圍陸城，嵩乃遣統軍封邁、王會等步騎八千討之。
manualTranslations.literal: Xiao Yan's Inspector of Xiangzhou Yang Gongze led twenty thousand men and stationed his army at Luokou; Jiang Qingzhen led five thousand soldiers and occupied Shoubei; and Yan also sent his Left Army General Qian Xiaoyan, army commanders He Tianzuo, Zhang Junxing, and others with seven thousand men to attack and surround Lucheng. Song then sent Commanders Feng Mai, Wang Hui, and others with eight thousand infantry and cavalry to attack them.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yang Gongze, Xiao Yan's Inspector of Xiangzhou, led twenty thousand men to Luokou; Jiang Qingzhen led five thousand to Shoubei; and Yan sent Left Army General Qian Xiaoyan, with army commanders He Tianzuo, Zhang Junxing, and others, leading seven thousand men to besiege Lucheng. Song sent Feng Mai, Wang Hui, and other commanders with eight thousand infantry and cavalry against them.

manualTranslations.zh: 邁達陸城，賊皆夜遁，追擊破之，斬獲數千，公則、慶真退還馬頭。
manualTranslations.literal: When Mai reached Lucheng, the rebels all fled by night; he pursued and defeated them, beheading and capturing several thousand, and Gongze and Qingzhen retreated back to Matou.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Feng Mai reached Lucheng, the rebels fled by night. He pursued and defeated them, killing or capturing several thousand, while Gongze and Qingzhen retreated to Matou.

manualTranslations.zh: 衍徐州刺史昌義之屯據高皇，遣三軍潛寇陰陵，以淮水淺竭，不通船艦，屯於馬頭。
manualTranslations.literal: Yan's Inspector of Xuzhou Chang Yizhi garrisoned and occupied Gaohuang, and sent three armies secretly to raid Yinling. Because the Huai water was shallow and exhausted and boats could not pass, he stationed at Matou.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Chang Yizhi, Yan's Inspector of Xuzhou, held Gaohuang and sent three armies in a secret raid on Yinling. Since the Huai was too shallow for boats to pass, he stationed at Matou.

manualTranslations.zh: 衍將田道龍、何景先等領卒三千已至衡山，規寇陸城。
manualTranslations.literal: Yan's generals Tian Daolong, He Jingxian, and others led three thousand soldiers and had already reached Hengshan, planning to raid Lucheng.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yan's generals Tian Daolong, He Jingxian, and others led three thousand soldiers to Hengshan, planning to raid Lucheng.

manualTranslations.zh: 寇並充逼。
manualTranslations.literal: The raiders were all pressing in densely.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The raiders pressed in from all sides.

manualTranslations.zh: 嵩遣兼統軍李叔仁等援合肥、小峴、楊石，頻戰破之。
manualTranslations.literal: Song sent acting Commander Li Shuren and others to reinforce Hefei, Xiaoxian, and Yangshi, and in repeated battles they defeated them.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Song sent acting Commander Li Shuren and others to reinforce Hefei, Xiaoxian, and Yangshi, repeatedly defeating the enemy in battle.

manualTranslations.zh: 衍征虜將軍趙草屯於黃口，嵩遣軍司趙熾等往討之，先遣統軍安伯醜潛師夜渡，伏兵下蔡。
manualTranslations.literal: Yan's General Who Conquers Caitiffs Zhao Cao was stationed at Huangkou. Song sent Army Marshal Zhao Chi and others to attack him, first sending Commander An Bochou to lead a hidden force across by night and place ambush troops at Xiacai.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Zhao Cao, Yan's General Who Conquers Caitiffs, was stationed at Huangkou. Song sent Army Marshal Zhao Chi and others to attack, first dispatching Commander An Bochou to cross secretly by night and set an ambush at Xiacai.

manualTranslations.zh: 草率卒四千，逆來拒戰，伯醜與下蔡戍主王虎等前後夾擊，大敗之，俘斬溺死四千餘人。
manualTranslations.literal: Cao led four thousand soldiers to come against them and resist in battle; Bochou and Wang Hu, commander of the Xiacai Garrison, attacked from front and rear and greatly defeated him, capturing, beheading, and drowning more than four thousand men.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Zhao Cao led four thousand men to meet them. An Bochou and Wang Hu, commander of Xiacai Garrison, struck from front and rear, badly defeated him, and captured, killed, or drowned more than four thousand men.

manualTranslations.zh: 統軍李叔仁等夜襲硤石之賊，又破之。
manualTranslations.literal: Commander Li Shuren and others made a night attack on the rebels at Xiashi and again defeated them.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Commander Li Shuren and others made a night attack on the rebels at Xiashi and defeated them as well.

manualTranslations.zh: 衍將姜慶真專據肥汭，冠軍將軍曹天寶屯於鷄口，軍主尹明世屯東硤石。
manualTranslations.literal: Yan's general Jiang Qingzhen alone occupied Feirui, Champion General Cao Tianbao was stationed at Jikou, and army commander Yin Mingshi was stationed at Eastern Xiashi.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yan's general Jiang Qingzhen held Feirui, Champion General Cao Tianbao was stationed at Jikou, and army commander Yin Mingshi at Eastern Xiashi.

manualTranslations.zh: 嵩遣別將羊引次于淮西，去賊營十里，司馬趙熾率兵一萬為表裏聲勢。
manualTranslations.literal: Song sent separate general Yang Yin to halt at Huaixi, ten li from the rebel camp, while Marshal Zhao Chi led ten thousand soldiers to form an inner and outer show of force.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Song sent the separate general Yang Yin to camp at Huaixi, ten li from the rebel camp, while Marshal Zhao Chi led ten thousand troops to create pressure from inside and outside.

manualTranslations.zh: 眾軍既會，分擊賊之四壘。
manualTranslations.literal: Once the various armies had assembled, they divided and attacked the rebels' four fortifications.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When the armies had assembled, they split up and attacked the rebels' four forts.

manualTranslations.zh: 四壘之賊，戰敗奔走，斬獲數千，溺死萬數。
manualTranslations.literal: The rebels in the four fortifications were defeated in battle and fled; several thousand were beheaded or captured, and those who drowned were counted by the ten thousand.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The rebels in the four forts were defeated and fled; several thousand were killed or captured, and tens of thousands drowned.

manualTranslations.zh: 統軍牛敬賓攻硤石，明世宵遁。
manualTranslations.literal: Commander Niu Jingbin attacked Xiashi, and Mingshi fled by night.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Commander Niu Jingbin attacked Xiashi, and Yin Mingshi fled by night.

manualTranslations.zh: 慶真合餘燼浮淮下，下蔡戍主王略截流擊之，俘斬太半。
manualTranslations.literal: Qingzhen gathered the remaining embers and floated down the Huai; Wang Lue, commander of the Xiacai Garrison, cut off the current and attacked him, capturing and beheading more than half.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Jiang Qingzhen gathered the remnants and moved down the Huai; Wang Lue, commander of Xiacai Garrison, intercepted him on the river and captured or killed more than half.

manualTranslations.zh: 於是威名大振。
manualTranslations.literal: Thereupon Song's awe-inspiring reputation greatly flourished.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Thereafter Song's reputation for military power greatly flourished.

manualTranslations.zh: 後為蒼頭李太伯等同謀害嵩，并妻穆氏及子世賢。
manualTranslations.literal: Later the cangtou Li Taibo and others conspired together and murdered Song, along with his wife Lady Mu and his son Shixian.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Later Li Taibo and other cangtou retainers conspired to murder Song, together with his wife Lady Mu and his son Shixian.

manualTranslations.zh: 世宗為嵩舉哀於東堂，賻絹一千匹，贈車騎將軍、領軍，諡曰剛侯。
manualTranslations.literal: Shizong raised mourning for Song in the Eastern Hall, gave one thousand bolts of silk for funeral expenses, posthumously granted him General of Chariots and Cavalry and Commander of the Guards, and gave him the posthumous title Marquis Gang.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Shizong held mourning for Song in the Eastern Hall, granted one thousand bolts of silk for the funeral, posthumously awarded him General of Chariots and Cavalry and Commander of the Guards, and gave him the posthumous title Marquis Gang.

manualTranslations.zh: 第二子世儁，頗有幹用，而無行業。
manualTranslations.literal: His second son Shijun had considerable practical ability, but no moral conduct.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: His second son Shijun had some practical ability but no moral conduct.

manualTranslations.zh: 襲爵，除給事中、東宮舍人。
manualTranslations.literal: He inherited the title and was appointed Supervising Attendant and Household Gentleman of the Eastern Palace.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He inherited the title and was appointed Supervising Attendant and Household Gentleman of the Eastern Palace.

manualTranslations.zh: 伯父澄表求轉階授之，於是除員外散騎常侍。
manualTranslations.literal: His uncle Cheng memorialized requesting that his rank be transferred and awarded to him, and thereupon he was appointed Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary Outside the Ranks.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: His uncle Cheng memorialized asking that a rank be transferred to him, and Shijun was appointed Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary Outside the Ranks.

manualTranslations.zh: 肅宗時，追論嵩勳，封世儁衞縣開國男，食邑二百戶。
manualTranslations.literal: In Suzong's time, Song's merit was retrospectively discussed, and Shijun was enfeoffed as Founding Baron of Wei County, with a fief of two hundred households.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In Suzong's reign, Song's merits were reviewed, and Shijun was enfeoffed as Founding Baron of Wei County with two hundred households.

manualTranslations.zh: 遷冠軍將軍、宗正少卿，又為散騎常侍、安南將軍、武衞將軍、河南尹。
manualTranslations.literal: He was promoted to Champion General and Junior Chamberlain for the Imperial Clan, and later became Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, General Who Pacifies the South, General of the Martial Guard, and Governor of Henan.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He rose to Champion General and Junior Chamberlain for the Imperial Clan, then served as Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, General Who Pacifies the South, General of the Martial Guard, and Governor of Henan.

manualTranslations.zh: 尋除鎮東將軍、青州刺史，轉征東將軍，加散騎常侍。
manualTranslations.literal: Soon he was appointed General Who Guards the East and Inspector of Qingzhou, transferred to General Who Conquers the East, and additionally made Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Soon he was appointed General Who Guards the East and Inspector of Qingzhou, then transferred to General Who Conquers the East with the added title Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary.

manualTranslations.zh: 邢杲之亂，圍逼州城，世儁憑城拒守，遂得保全。
manualTranslations.literal: During Xing Gao's rebellion, Gao surrounded and pressed the provincial city, and Shijun relied on the walls to resist and defend, so that it was preserved intact.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: During Xing Gao's rebellion, the provincial city was surrounded and pressed hard. Shijun held the walls and defended it, preserving the city intact.

manualTranslations.zh: 孝莊時，除衞將軍、吏部尚書。
manualTranslations.literal: In Emperor Xiaozhuang's time, he was appointed General of the Guard and Minister of Personnel.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In Emperor Xiaozhuang's reign, he was appointed General of the Guard and Minister of Personnel.

manualTranslations.zh: 爾朱兆寇京師，詔世儁以本官為都督，防守河橋。
manualTranslations.literal: When Erzhu Zhao raided the capital, an edict appointed Shijun, in his original office, as Commander-in-Chief to defend Heqiao.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Erzhu Zhao raided the capital, an edict kept Shijun in his current office and made him Commander-in-Chief for the defense of Heqiao.

manualTranslations.zh: 及兆至河，世儁初無拒守意，便隔岸遙拜，時論疾之。
manualTranslations.literal: When Zhao reached the river, Shijun from the start had no intention of resisting and defending, and at once bowed from across the bank; opinion at the time detested him.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Zhao reached the river, Shijun had no intention of resisting. He immediately bowed from across the bank, and public opinion despised him.

manualTranslations.zh: 前廢帝世，為驃騎將軍，仍加尚書，尤為爾朱世隆所昵。
manualTranslations.literal: In the reign of the Former Deposed Emperor, he was General of Agile Cavalry and was additionally made Minister of State Affairs; he was especially intimate with Erzhu Shilong.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Under the Former Deposed Emperor, he was General of Agile Cavalry with the added title Minister of State Affairs, and he was especially close to Erzhu Shilong.

manualTranslations.zh: 出帝初，加儀同三司，改封武陽縣開國子，食邑五百戶。
manualTranslations.literal: At the beginning of the reign of the Emperor Who Went Out, he was given Equal in Honor to the Three Excellencies, his enfeoffment was changed to Founding Viscount of Wuyang County, with a fief of five hundred households.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: At the start of the Emperor Who Went Out's reign, he was given Equal in Honor to the Three Excellencies and re-enfeoffed as Founding Viscount of Wuyang County with five hundred households.

manualTranslations.zh: 世儁居選曹，不能厲心，多所受納，為中尉彈糾，坐免官。
manualTranslations.literal: When Shijun occupied the selections bureau, he could not discipline his mind and accepted many gifts; he was impeached by the Censor-in-Chief and dismissed from office for the offense.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: While Shijun served in the selections bureau, he failed to discipline himself and accepted many gifts. The Censor-in-Chief impeached him, and he was dismissed.

manualTranslations.zh: 尋復本職。
manualTranslations.literal: Soon he was restored to his original office.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Soon he was restored to his former office.

manualTranslations.zh: 孝靜初，加侍中、尚書右僕射，遷尚書令。
manualTranslations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaojing's reign, he was given the added title Palace Attendant and Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, and was promoted to Director of the Department of State Affairs.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: At the start of Emperor Xiaojing's reign, he was made Palace Attendant and Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, then promoted to Director of the Department.

manualTranslations.zh: 世儁輕薄，好去就，詔送晉陽。
manualTranslations.literal: Shijun was frivolous and liked to shift his allegiances, so an edict sent him to Jinyang.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Shijun was frivolous and fond of shifting allegiance, so an edict sent him to Jinyang.

manualTranslations.zh: 興和中，薨。
manualTranslations.literal: In the Xinghe era, he died.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He died in the Xinghe era.

manualTranslations.zh: 贈侍中、都督冀定瀛殷四州諸軍事、驃騎大將軍、太傅、定州刺史，尚書令、開國公如故，諡曰躁戾。
manualTranslations.literal: He was posthumously granted Palace Attendant, Commander of all military affairs in Ji, Ding, Ying, and Yin provinces, Grand General of Agile Cavalry, Grand Tutor, and Inspector of Dingzhou; Director of the Department of State Affairs and Founding Duke remained as before; his posthumous title was Zaoli.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted Palace Attendant, Commander of all military affairs in Ji, Ding, Ying, and Yin provinces, Grand General of Agile Cavalry, Grand Tutor, and Inspector of Dingzhou, while retaining Director of the Department of State Affairs and Founding Duke as before. His posthumous title was Zaoli.

manualTranslations.zh: 子景遠襲，散騎侍郎。
manualTranslations.literal: His son Jingyuan succeeded; he was Cavalier Attendant.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: His son Jingyuan succeeded and served as Cavalier Attendant.

manualTranslations.zh: 世賢弟世哲，武定中，吏部郎。
manualTranslations.literal: Shixian's younger brother Shizhe, in the Wuding era, was Gentleman of the Ministry of Personnel.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Shixian's younger brother Shizhe served in the Wuding era as Gentleman of the Ministry of Personnel.

manualTranslations.zh: 嵩弟贍，字道周。
manualTranslations.literal: Song's younger brother Zhan was styled Daozhou.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Song's younger brother Zhan was styled Daozhou.

manualTranslations.zh: 高祖時，自□大夫稍遷宗正少卿、龍驤將軍、光州刺史、散騎常侍、左將軍，遷平東將軍、兗州刺史。
manualTranslations.literal: In Gaozu's time, from a Grandee title with one character missing he gradually rose to Junior Chamberlain for the Imperial Clan, Longxiang General, Inspector of Guangzhou, Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, and General of the Left, and was promoted to General Who Pacifies the East and Inspector of Yanzhou.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In Gaozu's time, from a Grandee title with one missing character, he gradually rose to Junior Chamberlain for the Imperial Clan, Longxiang General, Inspector of Guangzhou, Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, and General of the Left, then was promoted to General Who Pacifies the East and Inspector of Yanzhou.

manualTranslations.zh: 頗愛書史，而貪暴好殺。
manualTranslations.literal: He rather loved books and histories, but was greedy, violent, and fond of killing.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He had some love for books and histories, but was greedy, violent, and fond of killing.

manualTranslations.zh: 澄深恥忿之，絕其往來。
manualTranslations.literal: Cheng was deeply ashamed and angered by him and cut off dealings with him.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Cheng was deeply ashamed and angered by him and broke off all contact.

manualTranslations.zh: 有四子。
manualTranslations.literal: He had four sons.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He had four sons.

manualTranslations.zh: 長子遠，尚書郎。
manualTranslations.literal: The eldest son, Yuan, was a Gentleman of the Department of State Affairs.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The eldest son, Yuan, was a Gentleman of the Department of State Affairs.

manualTranslations.zh: 史臣曰：顯祖之將禪讓，可謂國之大節。
manualTranslations.literal: The historian says: When Xianzu was about to abdicate, it may be called a great joint of the state.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The historian says: When Xianzu was about to abdicate, it was a great test of the state.

manualTranslations.zh: 康王毅然庭諍，德音孔昭，一言興邦，其斯之謂歟？
manualTranslations.literal: Prince Kang firmly remonstrated in court, and his virtuous words were very bright; one word raised the state. Is this not what is meant?
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Prince Kang remonstrated firmly in court, his virtuous words shining clearly; one word raised the state. Is this not the phrase made real?

manualTranslations.zh: 文宣貞固俊遠，鬱為宗傑，身因累朝，寧濟夷險，既社稷是任，其梁棟之望也。
manualTranslations.literal: Wenxuan was upright, firm, outstanding, and far-reaching, richly becoming a hero of the imperial clan; in person he followed successive reigns, calmly crossing ease and danger, and since the altars of state were entrusted to him, he was the hope of beams and pillars.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Wenxuan was upright, firm, outstanding, and far-seeing, a flourishing hero of the imperial clan. Serving through successive reigns, calm in ease and danger, he bore responsibility for the state and was the hope of its beams and pillars.

manualTranslations.zh: 順謇諤俶儻，有汲黯之風，不用於時，橫招非命，惜矣。
manualTranslations.literal: Shun was blunt in remonstrance and free in spirit, with the manner of Ji An. Not used by his age, he unjustly met untimely death. A pity!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Shun was blunt and free-spirited, with the air of Ji An. Unused by his time, he wrongly met an untimely death. A pity!

manualTranslations.zh: 嵩有行陳之氣，儁則裂冠之徒歟？
manualTranslations.literal: Song had the spirit of the battle line, while Jun was the sort of man who tears the cap, was he not?
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Song had the spirit of the battle line; Jun was surely a cap-tearing sort of man, was he not?
