manualTranslations.literal: Cheng again memorialized that his mother was ill and asked to be relieved of his provincial office, but it was not permitted.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Cheng again memorialized that his mother was ill and asked to be relieved of his province, but this was not allowed.

manualTranslations.zh: 蕭衍將張囂之寇陷夷陵戍，澄遣輔國將軍成興步騎赴討，大破之，復夷陵，囂之遁走。
manualTranslations.literal: Xiao Yan's general Zhang Xiaozhi attacked and captured the Yiling Garrison; Cheng sent General Who Assists the State Cheng Xing with infantry and cavalry to go and attack him, greatly defeated him, recovered Yiling, and Xiaozhi fled.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Xiao Yan's general Zhang Xiaozhi captured the Yiling Garrison, Cheng sent Cheng Xing, General Who Assists the State, with infantry and cavalry to attack. Cheng Xing defeated him badly, recovered Yiling, and Xiaozhi fled.

manualTranslations.zh: 又遣長風戍主奇道顯攻蕭衍陰山戍，破之，斬其戍主龍驤將軍、都亭侯梅興祖。
manualTranslations.literal: He also sent Qi Daoxian, commander of the Changfeng Garrison, to attack Xiao Yan's Yinshan Garrison; he defeated it and beheaded its garrison commander, Mei Xingzu, General Who Rouses Dragons and Marquis of Duting.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He also sent Qi Daoxian, commander of Changfeng Garrison, to attack Xiao Yan's Yinshan Garrison. Qi defeated it and beheaded its commander Mei Xingzu, General Who Rouses Dragons and Marquis of Duting.

manualTranslations.zh: 仍引攻白槀戍，又破之，斬其寧朔將軍、關內侯吳道爽。
manualTranslations.literal: He then led the attack on Baigao Garrison, again defeated it, and beheaded its General Who Pacifies the North and Marquis within the Passes, Wu Daoshuang.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He then pressed on to attack Baigao Garrison, defeated it as well, and beheaded Wu Daoshuang, General Who Pacifies the North and Marquis within the Passes.

manualTranslations.zh: 澄表曰：「蕭衍頻斷東關，欲令巢湖汎溢。
manualTranslations.literal: Cheng memorialized, "Xiao Yan has repeatedly cut through Dongguan, wishing to make Chaohu overflow.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Cheng memorialized, "Xiao Yan has repeatedly breached Dongguan, intending to make Chaohu overflow.

manualTranslations.zh: 湖周回四百餘里，東關合江之際，廣不過數十步，若賊計得成，大湖傾注者，則淮南諸戍必同晉陽之事矣。
manualTranslations.literal: The lake is more than four hundred li around. Where Dongguan joins the river, its width is no more than several tens of paces. If the rebel plan succeeds and the great lake pours out, then all the Huainan garrisons will surely share the fate of Jinyang.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The lake is over four hundred li in circuit, and where Dongguan meets the river it is only a few dozen paces wide. If the rebels succeed and the great lake pours out, all our Huainan garrisons will suffer the fate of Jinyang.

manualTranslations.zh: 又吳楚便水，且灌且掠，淮南之地，將非國有。
manualTranslations.literal: Moreover, Wu and Chu are adept at water; flooding as they plunder, the lands of Huainan will no longer belong to the state.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Moreover, Wu and Chu are skilled in water warfare. If they flood while raiding, Huainan will no longer be ours.

manualTranslations.zh: 壽陽去江五百餘里，眾庶惶惶，並懼水害。
manualTranslations.literal: Shouyang is more than five hundred li from the river, and the masses are anxious and afraid, all fearing the harm of water.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Shouyang lies more than five hundred li from the river, and the people are terrified, all fearing flood damage.

manualTranslations.zh: 脫乘民之願，攻敵之虛，豫勒諸州，纂集士馬，首秋大集，則南瀆可為飲馬之津，霍嶺必成徙倚之觀，事貴應機，經略須早。
manualTranslations.literal: If we take advantage of the people's wishes and attack the enemy's emptiness, prearrange the provinces, gather soldiers and horses, and assemble them at the beginning of autumn, then the southern channel may become a ford where we water horses, and Huo Ridge will surely become a lookout where we linger. Affairs value response to opportunity, and planning must be early.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: If we use the people's wishes, strike the enemy's weak point, prearrange the provinces, gather troops and horses, and assemble them in early autumn, then the southern channel can become a ford for watering our horses, and Huo Ridge a height from which we look out at ease. Opportunity must be answered, and planning must begin early.

manualTranslations.zh: 縱混一不可必果，江西自是無虞。
manualTranslations.literal: Even if complete unification cannot be certainly achieved, the west of the Yangzi will naturally be without worry.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Even if complete unification cannot be guaranteed, the lands west of the Yangzi will at least be secure.

manualTranslations.zh: 若猶豫緩圖，不加除討，關塞既成，襄陵方及，平原民戍定為魚矣。」
manualTranslations.literal: If we still hesitate and slowly make plans, without adding removal and punishment, once the passes and barriers are completed and the waters reach the hills, the people and garrisons of the plains will certainly become fish."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: If we hesitate and delay instead of eliminating the threat, then once the barriers are finished and the waters rise to the hills, the people and garrisons of the plains will become fish."

manualTranslations.zh: 詔發冀、定、瀛、相、并、濟六州二萬人，馬一千五百匹，令仲秋之中畢會淮南，并壽陽先兵三萬，委澄經略。
manualTranslations.literal: An edict mobilized twenty thousand men and one thousand five hundred horses from the six provinces of Ji, Ding, Ying, Xiang, Bing, and Ji, ordering them all to assemble in Huainan by mid-autumn; together with Shouyang's previous thirty thousand troops, they were entrusted to Cheng for planning.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: An edict mobilized twenty thousand men and fifteen hundred horses from Ji, Ding, Ying, Xiang, Bing, and Ji provinces, ordering them to assemble in Huainan by mid-autumn. Together with Shouyang's existing thirty thousand troops, they were placed under Cheng's command.

manualTranslations.zh: 先是朝議有南伐之意，以蕭寶夤為東揚州刺史據東城，陳伯之為江州刺史戍陽石，以澄總督二鎮，授之節度。
manualTranslations.literal: Before this, the court deliberations had intended a southern campaign, appointing Xiao Baoyin Inspector of Eastern Yangzhou to occupy Dongcheng and Chen Bozhi Inspector of Jiangzhou to garrison Yangshi; Cheng was made commander-in-chief of the two garrisons and given authority over their commands.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Earlier, the court had planned a southern campaign, placing Xiao Baoyin at Dongcheng as Inspector of Eastern Yangzhou and Chen Bozhi at Yangshi as Inspector of Jiangzhou. Cheng was put in overall command of the two positions.

manualTranslations.zh: 至是勒兵進討。
manualTranslations.literal: At this point he ordered the troops forward to attack.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: At this point he ordered the troops forward.

manualTranslations.zh: 以東關水衝，大峴險要，東關縱水，陽石、合肥有急懸之切，不圖大峴，則歷陽有乘險之援，淮陵陸道，九山水路，並宜經略。
manualTranslations.literal: Because Dongguan was the water choke point and Daxian was a strategic pass, if Dongguan released water, Yangshi and Hefei would face an urgent suspended danger; if Daxian was not planned for, then Liyang would have support by using the pass. The land route through Huailing and the water route through Jiushan both had to be planned for.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Dongguan controlled the water flow, and Daxian was a crucial pass. If Dongguan released the water, Yangshi and Hefei would be in immediate danger; if Daxian was ignored, Liyang could use the pass as support. The Huailing land route and the Jiushan water route both had to be included in the plan.

manualTranslations.zh: 於是遣統軍傅豎眼、王神念等進次大峴、東關、九山、淮陵，皆分部諸將，倍道據之，總勒大眾，絡繹相接。
manualTranslations.literal: Thereupon he sent Commanders Fu Shuyan, Wang Shennian, and others to advance and camp at Daxian, Dongguan, Jiushan, and Huailing. All divided the generals by sections, marched by double stages to occupy them, and brought the great host under command, one unit after another in continuous connection.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He therefore sent Fu Shuyan, Wang Shennian, and other commanders to advance to Daxian, Dongguan, Jiushan, and Huailing. The generals divided the sectors, hurried to occupy them, and linked the main forces in a continuous line.

manualTranslations.zh: 而神念克其關要、潁川二城，斬衍軍主費尼。
manualTranslations.literal: Shennian captured the two cities of Guanyao and Yingchuan and beheaded Xiao Yan's army commander Fei Ni.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Wang Shennian captured Guanyao and Yingchuan and beheaded Fei Ni, one of Xiao Yan's commanders.

manualTranslations.zh: 而寧朔將軍韋惠、龍驤將軍李伯由仍固大峴。
manualTranslations.literal: Ning Shuo General Wei Hui and Longxiang General Li Boyou still firmly held Daxian.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Ning Shuo General Wei Hui and Longxiang General Li Boyou were still holding Daxian.

manualTranslations.zh: 澄遣統軍党法宗、傅豎眼等進軍克之，遂圍白塔、牽城，數日之間，便即逃潰。
manualTranslations.literal: Cheng sent Commanders Dang Fazong, Fu Shuyan, and others to advance their armies and take it. They then surrounded Baita and Qiancheng, and within several days these immediately fled and collapsed.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Cheng sent Dang Fazong, Fu Shuyan, and other commanders forward to take it. They then besieged Baita and Qiancheng, which fled and collapsed within a few days.

manualTranslations.zh: 衍清溪戍望風散走。
manualTranslations.literal: Xiao Yan's Qingxi Garrison scattered and fled at the sight of their momentum.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Xiao Yan's Qingxi Garrison scattered at the news.

manualTranslations.zh: 衍徐州刺史司馬明素率眾三千，欲援九山；
manualTranslations.literal: Xiao Yan's Inspector of Xuzhou Sima Mingsu led three thousand men, wishing to reinforce Jiushan;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Sima Mingsu, Xiao Yan's Inspector of Xuzhou, led three thousand men to reinforce Jiushan;

manualTranslations.zh: 徐州長史潘伯隣規固淮陵；
manualTranslations.literal: Pan Bolin, Chief Clerk of Xuzhou, planned to hold Huailing;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Pan Bolin, Chief Clerk of Xuzhou, planned to hold Huailing;

manualTranslations.zh: 寧朔將軍王燮負險焦城。
manualTranslations.literal: Ning Shuo General Wang Xie relied on the defenses of Jiaocheng.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: and Ning Shuo General Wang Xie relied on the strong position at Jiaocheng.

manualTranslations.zh: 法宗進克焦城，破淮陵，擒明素，斬伯隣。
manualTranslations.literal: Fazong advanced, captured Jiaocheng, broke Huailing, captured Mingsu, and beheaded Bolin.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Dang Fazong advanced, captured Jiaocheng, broke Huailing, captured Mingsu, and beheaded Bolin.

manualTranslations.zh: 其濟陰太守王厚強、廬江太守裴邃即亦奔退。
manualTranslations.literal: Their Governor of Jiyin Wang Houqiang and Governor of Lujiang Pei Sui then also fled in retreat.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Wang Houqiang, their Governor of Jiyin, and Pei Sui, Governor of Lujiang, also fled.

manualTranslations.zh: 詔澄曰：「將軍文德內昭，武功外暢，奮揚大略，將蕩江吳。
manualTranslations.literal: The edict to Cheng said, "General, your civil virtue shines within and your military achievement spreads without; you raise and display grand strategy and are about to sweep away Jiang and Wu.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The edict to Cheng said, "General, your civil virtue shines within and your military achievements resound abroad. You have displayed a grand strategy and are about to sweep away Jiang and Wu.

manualTranslations.zh: 長旌始舒，賊徒懾氣，銳旅方馳，東關席卷。
manualTranslations.literal: When the long banners first unfurled, the rebel followers lost heart; as the sharp troops were only beginning to race forward, Dongguan was swept up like a mat.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: As soon as the long banners were unfurled, the rebels lost heart; as the elite troops began to advance, Dongguan was rolled up like a mat.

manualTranslations.zh: 想江湖弭波，在旦夕耳。
manualTranslations.literal: I expect the rivers and lakes will calm their waves in the space of morning and evening.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: I expect the rivers and lakes to be pacified very soon.

manualTranslations.zh: 所送首虜，並已聞之。」
manualTranslations.literal: The heads and captives you sent have all been reported."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The heads and captives you sent have all been reported."

manualTranslations.zh: 初，澄出討之後，衍將姜慶真襲據壽春外郭，齊王蕭寶夤擊走之。
manualTranslations.literal: At first, after Cheng went out to attack, Xiao Yan's general Jiang Qingzhen attacked and occupied the outer wall of Shouchun, and Xiao Baoyin, Prince of Qi, attacked and drove him off.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Earlier, after Cheng had marched out, Xiao Yan's general Jiang Qingzhen attacked and occupied the outer wall of Shouchun, but Xiao Baoyin, Prince of Qi, attacked and drove him away.

manualTranslations.zh: 長史韋纘坐免官，澄以在外無坐。
manualTranslations.literal: Chief Clerk Wei Zuan was dismissed from office for the offense, while Cheng, because he was away, was not implicated.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Chief Clerk Wei Zuan was dismissed for this, while Cheng was not held responsible because he was away.

manualTranslations.zh: 遂攻鍾離。
manualTranslations.literal: He then attacked Zhongli.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Cheng then attacked Zhongli.

manualTranslations.zh: 又詔：「鍾離若食盡，三月已前，固有可克，如至四月，淮水泛長，舟行無礙，宜善量之。
manualTranslations.literal: Another edict said, "If Zhongli exhausts its food, before the third month it can certainly be taken; if it reaches the fourth month, the Huai waters will rise and swell, and boats will move without obstruction. You should measure this well.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Another edict said, "If Zhongli runs out of food, it can surely be taken before the third month; but if matters reach the fourth month, the Huai will rise and boats will pass freely. Weigh this carefully.

manualTranslations.zh: 前事捷也，此實將軍經略，勳有常焉。
manualTranslations.literal: The previous success was truly the result of your planning, General, and the merit has its constant place.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The earlier victory was truly due to your planning, General, and that merit stands secure.

manualTranslations.zh: 如或以水盛難圖，亦可為萬全之計，不宜昧利無成，以貽後悔也。」
manualTranslations.literal: If perhaps the high water makes it difficult to plan, you may also make a plan of complete safety. It is not fitting to be blinded by advantage, achieve nothing, and leave later regret."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: If high water makes the objective difficult, you may choose a safer plan. Do not be blinded by advantage, fail to achieve the goal, and leave regret for later."

manualTranslations.zh: 蕭衍冠軍將軍張惠紹，游擊將軍殷暹、驍騎將軍趙景悅、龍驤將軍張景仁等率眾五千，送糧鍾離。
manualTranslations.literal: Xiao Yan's General Who Conquers Champions Zhang Huishao, General of Mobile Assault Yin Xian, General of Valiant Cavalry Zhao Jingyue, Longxiang General Zhang Jingren, and others led five thousand men to send grain to Zhongli.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Xiao Yan's generals Zhang Huishao, Yin Xian, Zhao Jingyue, Zhang Jingren, and others led five thousand men escorting grain to Zhongli.

manualTranslations.zh: 澄遣統軍王足、劉思祖等邀擊惠紹等，大破之。
manualTranslations.literal: Cheng sent Commanders Wang Zu, Liu Sizu, and others to intercept and strike Huishao and the others, greatly defeating them.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Cheng sent Wang Zu, Liu Sizu, and other commanders to intercept Huishao and his men, defeating them badly.

manualTranslations.zh: 獲惠紹、殷暹、景仁及其屯騎校尉史文淵等軍主以上二十七人。
manualTranslations.literal: They captured Huishao, Yin Xian, Jingren, and Shi Wenyuan, their Colonel of Garrison Cavalry, along with twenty-seven men of army commander rank and above.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: They captured Huishao, Yin Xian, Jingren, Shi Wenyuan, their Colonel of Garrison Cavalry, and twenty-seven officers of army commander rank or higher.

manualTranslations.zh: 既而遇雨，淮水暴長，引歸壽春。
manualTranslations.literal: Afterward, they met with rain, the Huai waters suddenly rose, and he withdrew back to Shouchun.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Soon afterward rain came, the Huai rose sharply, and Cheng withdrew to Shouchun.

manualTranslations.zh: 還既狼狽，失兵四千餘人。
manualTranslations.literal: Once the return had become disorderly, he lost more than four thousand soldiers.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The retreat became disordered, and he lost more than four thousand men.

manualTranslations.zh: 頻表解州，世宗不許。
manualTranslations.literal: He repeatedly memorialized asking to be relieved of his province, but Shizong did not permit it.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He repeatedly memorialized asking to be relieved of his province, but Shizong refused.

manualTranslations.zh: 有司奏軍還失路，奪其開府，又降三階。
manualTranslations.literal: The responsible offices memorialized that the army had lost the road on its return; his open office was taken away, and he was further lowered three ranks.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The officials memorialized that the returning army had lost its route; Cheng was stripped of his open office and demoted three ranks.

manualTranslations.zh: 時蕭衍有移，求換張惠紹。
manualTranslations.literal: At the time Xiao Yan had sent an official letter requesting an exchange for Zhang Huishao.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: At the time Xiao Yan sent a letter requesting an exchange for Zhang Huishao.

manualTranslations.zh: 澄表請不許，詔付八座會議。
manualTranslations.literal: Cheng memorialized requesting that this not be permitted, and an edict referred it to the Eight Seats for joint discussion.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Cheng memorialized that the request should not be allowed, and the edict referred it to the Eight Seats for conference.

manualTranslations.zh: 尚書令、廣陽王嘉等奏宜還之，詔乃聽還。
manualTranslations.literal: Director of the Department of State Affairs Jia, Prince of Guangyang, and others memorialized that he should be returned, and the edict then permitted the return.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Jia, Prince of Guangyang and Director of the Department of State Affairs, and others memorialized that Zhang Huishao should be returned, and the edict allowed it.

manualTranslations.zh: 後果復寇邊。
manualTranslations.literal: Later, as expected, he again raided the border.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Later, as expected, he raided the border again.

manualTranslations.zh: 轉澄鎮北大將軍、定州刺史。
manualTranslations.literal: Cheng was transferred to Grand General Who Guards the North and Inspector of Dingzhou.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Cheng was transferred to Grand General Who Guards the North and Inspector of Dingzhou.

manualTranslations.zh: 初，民中每有橫調，百姓煩苦，前後牧守，未能蠲除，澄多所省減，民以忻賴。
manualTranslations.literal: At first, whenever there were arbitrary levies among the people, the common people were troubled and suffering. The governors and administrators before and after him had not been able to remove them, but Cheng reduced many of them, and the people joyfully relied on him.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The people had long suffered from arbitrary levies, which previous governors and administrators had failed to abolish. Cheng reduced many of them, and the people rejoiced and relied on him.

manualTranslations.zh: 又明黜陟賞罰之法，表減公園之地，以給無業貧口，禁造布絹不任衣者。
manualTranslations.literal: He also clarified the laws of demotion and promotion, reward and punishment, memorialized to reduce the land of public parks in order to give it to poor households without occupations, and prohibited the making of cloth and silk not fit for clothing.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He also clarified rules for promotion, demotion, reward, and punishment; memorialized to reduce public parkland and give it to poor households without livelihoods; and banned the production of cloth and silk unfit for clothing.

manualTranslations.zh: 母孟太妃薨，居喪毀瘠，當世稱之。
manualTranslations.literal: When his mother, Grand Consort Meng, died, his mourning left him wasted and thin, and the age praised him.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When his mother, Grand Consort Meng, died, he wasted away in mourning, and his contemporaries praised him for it.

manualTranslations.zh: 服闋，除太子太保。
manualTranslations.literal: When the mourning period was complete, he was appointed Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: After the mourning period ended, he was appointed Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

manualTranslations.zh: 於時高肇當朝，猜忌賢戚。
manualTranslations.literal: At that time Gao Zhao controlled the court and was suspicious and jealous of worthy imperial relatives.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: At that time Gao Zhao controlled the court and was suspicious of worthy imperial relatives.

manualTranslations.zh: 澄為肇間構，常恐不全，乃終日昏飲，以示荒敗。
manualTranslations.literal: Cheng was estranged and framed by Zhao, and constantly feared he would not be preserved; he therefore drank muddily all day to show ruin and failure.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Cheng was slandered and isolated by Gao Zhao and constantly feared for his life, so he drank heavily all day to appear ruined and useless.

manualTranslations.zh: 所作詭越，時謂為狂。
manualTranslations.literal: The strange and excessive things he did were called madness at the time.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: His strange, excessive behavior was taken at the time for madness.

manualTranslations.zh: 世宗夜崩，時事倉卒，高肇擁兵於外，肅宗沖幼，朝野不安。
manualTranslations.literal: Shizong died at night, events were urgent and confused, Gao Zhao held troops outside, Suzong was young, and court and countryside were unsettled.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Shizong died at night, events were sudden and confused. Gao Zhao held troops outside, Suzong was still a child, and both court and countryside were uneasy.

manualTranslations.zh: 澄疏斥不預機要，而朝望所屬，領軍于忠、侍中崔光等奏澄為尚書令，於是眾心忻服。
manualTranslations.literal: Cheng had been distantly rejected and did not take part in the essentials of policy, yet the hopes of the court rested on him. Commander of the Guards Yu Zhong, Palace Attendant Cui Guang, and others memorialized that Cheng be made Director of the Department of State Affairs, and at this the hearts of the multitude joyfully submitted.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Cheng had been kept at a distance and excluded from confidential affairs, but the court's hopes rested on him. Yu Zhong, Commander of the Guards, Cui Guang, Palace Attendant, and others memorialized that Cheng be made Director of the Department of State Affairs, and everyone gladly accepted this.

manualTranslations.zh: 又加散騎常侍、驃騎大將軍，尋遷司空，加侍中，俄詔領尚書令。
manualTranslations.literal: He was also made Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary and Grand General of Agile Cavalry; soon he was transferred to Minister of Works and given the added title Palace Attendant, and shortly afterward an edict had him concurrently direct the Department of State Affairs.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He was also made Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary and Grand General of Agile Cavalry; soon he was promoted to Minister of Works with the added title Palace Attendant, and shortly afterward was ordered to concurrently direct the Department of State Affairs.

manualTranslations.zh: 初，正始之末，詔百司普昇一級，而執事者不達旨意，刺史、守、令限而不及。
manualTranslations.literal: Earlier, at the end of the Zhengshi era, an edict had raised all the offices by one grade, but those handling the matter did not understand the intent, so inspectors, governors, and magistrates were limited and did not receive it.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Earlier, at the end of the Zhengshi era, an edict raised all offices by one grade, but the officials implementing it misunderstood the intent, so inspectors, governors, and magistrates were excluded.

manualTranslations.zh: 澄奏曰：「竊惟雲構鬱起，澤及百司，企春望榮，內外同慶。
manualTranslations.literal: Cheng memorialized, "I privately consider that the cloud-built grace rose richly and its favor reached the hundred offices; looking toward spring and hoping for glory, inner and outer officials celebrated together.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Cheng memorialized, "I humbly think that when imperial favor rose like gathering clouds and reached the hundred offices, officials inside and outside the court looked toward renewed honor and rejoiced together.

manualTranslations.zh: 至於賞陟，不及守宰，爾來十年，冤訟不絕。
manualTranslations.literal: But when it came to rewarding advancement, it did not reach governors and magistrates, and for ten years since then grievances and lawsuits have not ceased.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yet the promotion did not reach governors and magistrates, and for ten years grievances and appeals have continued without end.

manualTranslations.zh: 封回自鎮遠、安州入為太尉長史，元匡自征虜、恒州入作宗卿，二人遷授，並在先詔。
manualTranslations.literal: Feng Hui entered from General Who Guards Afar and Anzhou to become Chief Clerk to the Grand Commandant; Yuan Kuang entered from General Who Conquers Caitiffs and Hengzhou to become Chamberlain for the Imperial Clan. The promotions and appointments of these two men were both before the earlier edict.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Feng Hui came in from Zhenyuan General and Anzhou to serve as Chief Clerk to the Grand Commandant, while Yuan Kuang came in from Zhenglu General and Hengzhou to serve as Chamberlain for the Imperial Clan. Both appointments occurred before the earlier edict.

manualTranslations.zh: 應蒙之理，備在於斯。
manualTranslations.literal: The principle that they should receive the benefit is fully present in these cases.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: These cases fully show the principle by which they should receive the benefit.

manualTranslations.zh: 兼州佐停私之徒，陪臣郡丞之例，尚蒙天澤下降，榮及當時。
manualTranslations.literal: In addition, provincial assistants, those who had suspended private service, subordinate ministers, and commandery deputies still received the descent of heavenly favor, and the honor reached them at the time.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Moreover, provincial assistants, private retainers who had ceased service, subordinate officers, and commandery deputies all received the court's favor and shared in the honor at the time.

manualTranslations.zh: 然參佐之來，皆因府主，今府主不霑，佐官獨預，棄本賞末，愚謂未允。
manualTranslations.literal: Yet assistants come in all because of their office heads. Now the office heads do not receive the favor, while assistant officials alone participate; abandoning the root and rewarding the branch, in my foolish opinion, is not fair.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: But assistants come forward through their chiefs. For the chiefs to receive nothing while their subordinates alone benefit abandons the root and rewards the branch; in my foolish view this is not just.

manualTranslations.zh: 今計刺史、守、宰之官，請準回匡，悉同汎限，上允初旨百司之章，下覆訟者元元之心。」
manualTranslations.literal: Now, calculating the offices of inspectors, governors, and magistrates, I request that they be modeled on Hui and Kuang and all be included within the general limit, above fulfilling the original edict's phrase "the hundred offices," and below answering the hearts of the common people who have appealed."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: I therefore ask that inspectors, governors, and magistrates be treated according to the precedents of Feng Hui and Yuan Kuang and included within the general scope, above fulfilling the original edict's words about the hundred offices, and below satisfying the hearts of the people who have appealed."

manualTranslations.zh: 詔曰：「自今已後，內外之事，嘗經先朝者，不得重聞。」
manualTranslations.literal: The edict said, "From now on, matters inside and outside the court that once passed through the former reign may not be reported again."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The edict said, "From now on, internal and external matters already handled under the former reign may not be reported again."

manualTranslations.zh: 澄奏曰：「臣聞堯懸諫諍之鼓，舜置誹謗之木，皆所以廣耳目於芻蕘，達四聰於天下。
manualTranslations.literal: Cheng memorialized, "I have heard that Yao hung the drum for remonstrance and Shun set up the wood for criticism; both were means to broaden ears and eyes among woodcutters and herdsmen and make the fourfold hearing reach all under Heaven.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Cheng memorialized, "I have heard that Yao hung up the remonstrance drum and Shun set up the criticism post, both to widen their hearing and sight among even the humblest people and let the ruler's fourfold hearing reach all under Heaven.

manualTranslations.zh: 伏惟太祖開基，化隆自遠，累聖相承，於今九帝。
manualTranslations.literal: I bow and consider that Taizu opened the foundation and his transformation flourished from afar; successive sages have inherited one another, now reaching nine emperors.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Taizu founded the dynasty and his transforming rule spread far. Sage rulers have succeeded one another, down to the ninth emperor today.

manualTranslations.zh: 重光疊照，汚隆必同，與奪隨時，道無恒體。
manualTranslations.literal: Repeated radiance and layered illumination, decline and flourishing must all be the same; granting and taking follow the time, and the Way has no constant form.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Their radiance has shone one after another; whether in decline or flourishing, the principle is the same. Granting and withholding follow the times, and the Way has no fixed form.

manualTranslations.zh: 思過如渴，言重千金，故稱無諱之朝，邁蹤三、五。
manualTranslations.literal: They thirsted to think on faults and valued words at a thousand in gold; therefore ours was called a court without taboos, surpassing the tracks of the Three and Five.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: They thirsted for reflection on their faults and valued speech at a thousand pieces of gold; thus ours was called a court without taboos, surpassing the Three Sovereigns and Five Emperors.

manualTranslations.zh: 高祖沖年纂曆，文明協統，變官易律，未為違典。
manualTranslations.literal: Gaozu succeeded to the calendar at a tender age, and Wenming cooperated in rule; they changed offices and altered laws, but this did not violate the classics.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Gaozu inherited the throne while young, and Empress Wenming assisted the government. They changed offices and laws, yet did not violate classical norms.

manualTranslations.zh: 及慈聖臨朝，母儀宇縣，爰發慈令，垂心滯獄，深枉者仰日月於九泉，微屈者希曲照於盆下。
manualTranslations.literal: When the Compassionate Sage held court, her maternal model covered the realm; she then issued compassionate orders and set her heart on delayed lawsuits, so those deeply wronged looked up to the sun and moon from the Nine Springs, and those slightly aggrieved hoped for a bent light beneath the overturned basin.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When the Compassionate Sage held court, her maternal example covered the realm. She issued merciful orders and attended to stalled cases, so the deeply wronged looked up to sun and moon even from the Nine Springs, and the slightly aggrieved hoped for a slant of light beneath the overturned basin.

manualTranslations.zh: 今乃格以先朝，限以一例，斯誠奉遵之本心，實乖元元之至望。
manualTranslations.literal: Now to bar them by saying "the former reign" and limit them by a single rule truly follows the root intention of obedience, but in fact goes against the utmost hopes of the common people.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Now to block such cases as belonging to the former reign and limit them by one rule may be meant as obedience, but it truly violates the people's deepest hopes.

manualTranslations.zh: 在于謙挹，有乖舊典。
manualTranslations.literal: In humility and yielding, it departs from the old institutions.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: As a matter of humble receptiveness, it also departs from the old institutions.

manualTranslations.zh: 謹尋抱枉求直，或經累朝。
manualTranslations.literal: I have carefully examined those who hold grievances and seek straightening; some have passed through several reigns.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: I have examined those who carry grievances and seek justice; some cases have lasted through several reigns.

manualTranslations.zh: 毫釐之差，正之宜速；
manualTranslations.literal: A difference of a hair or a li should be corrected quickly;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: A difference of a hair's breadth should be corrected quickly;

manualTranslations.zh: 謬若千里，駟馬弗追。
manualTranslations.literal: if the error is like a thousand li, even a team of four horses cannot catch it.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: if an error becomes a thousand li, even a four-horse team cannot catch it.

manualTranslations.zh: 故禮有損益，事有可否，父有諍子，君有諫臣，琴瑟不調，理宜改作。
manualTranslations.literal: Therefore ritual has diminutions and additions, affairs have what may and may not be done, fathers have sons who contest them, and rulers have ministers who remonstrate with them. If zithers and lutes are not in tune, principle says they should be adjusted.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Thus ritual can be reduced or augmented, affairs can be approved or rejected, fathers have sons who argue with them, and rulers have ministers who remonstrate. If zithers and lutes are out of tune, they should be adjusted.

manualTranslations.zh: 是以防川之論，小決則通；
manualTranslations.literal: Thus in the argument about blocking rivers, a small opening lets them flow;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Thus, in the argument over blocking rivers, a small opening lets them flow;

manualTranslations.zh: 鄉校之言，擁則敗國。
manualTranslations.literal: as for speech in the village schools, if it is blocked, it ruins the state.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: and as for speech in the village schools, blocking it ruins the state.

manualTranslations.zh: 矧伊陳屈，而可抑以先朝。
manualTranslations.literal: How much more when they are setting forth grievances: how can they be suppressed by saying "the former reign"?
manualTranslations.idiomatic: How much more when people are presenting grievances: how can they be suppressed merely because they concern a former reign?

manualTranslations.zh: 且先朝屈者，非故屈之，或有司愛憎，或執事濁僻，空文致法，以誤視聽。
manualTranslations.literal: Moreover, those wronged under the former reign were not intentionally wronged. Sometimes there was love or hatred by the offices, sometimes murky partiality among those handling matters, and empty documents brought about law, thereby misleading hearing and sight.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Those wronged under the former reign were not wronged deliberately by the throne. Sometimes officials were moved by favoritism or hatred, sometimes clerks were corrupt and biased, and empty paperwork produced legal judgments that misled the court.

manualTranslations.zh: 如此冤塞，彌在可哀。
manualTranslations.literal: Such blocked grievances are all the more worthy of pity.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Such obstructed grievances are all the more pitiful.

manualTranslations.zh: 僭之與濫，寧失不經，乞收今旨，還依前詔。」
manualTranslations.literal: As for overstepping and excess, I would rather err on the side of irregularity; I beg that the present order be withdrawn and that we return to following the previous edict."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: If there is risk of excess, I would rather err on the side of irregular openness. I beg that the present order be withdrawn and that we return to the previous edict."

manualTranslations.zh: 詔曰：「省奏，深體毗贊之情，三皇異軌，五代殊風，一時之制，何必詮改。
manualTranslations.literal: The edict said, "I have reviewed the memorial and deeply understand the feeling of assisting and supporting. The Three Sovereigns had different tracks and the Five Ages different customs; why must the institutions of one time all be weighed and changed?
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The edict said, "I have reviewed the memorial and deeply understand your wish to assist the throne. The Three Sovereigns followed different paths and the Five Ages different customs; why must the institutions of one period all be revised?

manualTranslations.zh: 必謂虛文設旨，理在可申者，何容不同來執。
manualTranslations.literal: If it is necessarily said that empty texts set forth intentions and that the principle lies in what can be extended, how could we allow them not all to come and be taken up alike?
manualTranslations.idiomatic: If one says that formal texts merely express an intention and that the principle may be extended, then how could similar cases not all come forward to be taken up?

manualTranslations.zh: 可依往制。」
manualTranslations.literal: It may follow the former system."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Let the former system be followed."

manualTranslations.zh: 澄表上皇誥宗制并訓詁各一卷，意欲皇太后覽之，思勸戒之益。
manualTranslations.literal: Cheng submitted one fascicle each of Imperial Admonitions, Clan Regulations, and Explanatory Glosses, intending that the Empress Dowager read them and consider their benefit for exhortation and warning.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Cheng submitted one fascicle each of Imperial Admonitions, Clan Regulations, and Explanatory Glosses, hoping the Empress Dowager would read them and consider their value for admonition.

manualTranslations.zh: 又奏利國濟民所宜振舉者十條。
manualTranslations.literal: He also memorialized ten articles on what should be revived and promoted to benefit the state and aid the people.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He also submitted ten recommendations for measures that should be revived to benefit the state and aid the people.

manualTranslations.zh: 一曰律度量衡，公私不同，所宜一之。
manualTranslations.literal: The first said: laws, measures, weights, and balances differ between public and private use; they should be unified.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: First: statutes, measures, weights, and balances differ between public and private use and should be unified.

manualTranslations.zh: 二曰宜興學校，以明黜陟之法。
manualTranslations.literal: The second said: schools should be promoted in order to clarify the law of demotion and promotion.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Second: schools should be promoted to clarify the rules for demotion and promotion.

manualTranslations.zh: 三曰宜興滅繼絕，各舉所知。
manualTranslations.literal: The third said: what has perished should be revived and extinct lines continued, and each should recommend those he knows.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Third: fallen lines should be revived and extinct lines continued, with each official recommending those he knows.

manualTranslations.zh: 四曰五調之外，一不煩民，任民之力，不過三日。
manualTranslations.literal: The fourth said: beyond the five levies, the people should not be troubled at all, and use of the people's labor should not exceed three days.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Fourth: beyond the five regular levies, the people should not be burdened, and labor service should not exceed three days.

manualTranslations.zh: 五曰臨民之官，皆須黜陟，以旌賞罰。
manualTranslations.literal: The fifth said: officials who govern the people must all be demoted or promoted in order to make rewards and punishments clear.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Fifth: officials who govern the people must be subject to promotion and demotion, so that reward and punishment are clear.

manualTranslations.zh: 六曰逃亡代輸，去來年久者，若非伎作，任聽即住。
manualTranslations.literal: The sixth said: for fugitives whose dues are paid by substitutes, and whose coming and going has lasted many years, if they are not artisans, they should be freely allowed to settle where they are.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Sixth: fugitives whose obligations are being paid by substitutes, and whose absence or return has lasted for years, should be allowed to settle where they are, unless they are registered artisans.

manualTranslations.zh: 七曰邊兵逃走，或實陷沒，皆須精檢；
manualTranslations.literal: The seventh said: border soldiers who flee, or who in fact have fallen or been lost, must all be carefully examined;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Seventh: cases of border soldiers who flee, or who have truly been captured or killed, must be carefully investigated;

manualTranslations.zh: 三長及近親，若實隱之，徵其代輸，不隱勿論。
manualTranslations.literal: if the three chiefs and close kin have truly concealed it, collect substitute payments from them; if they did not conceal it, do not prosecute them.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: if the three chiefs or close relatives truly concealed the facts, collect the substitute payments from them; if they did not conceal them, do not prosecute.

manualTranslations.zh: 八曰工商世業之戶，復徵租調，無以堪濟，今請免之，使專其業。
manualTranslations.literal: The eighth said: households whose hereditary occupations are crafts and commerce are again being charged rents and levies and have no means to endure and meet them. I now request that they be exempted, so that they may specialize in their occupations.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Eighth: hereditary artisan and merchant households are again being charged rents and levies beyond what they can bear. I request that they be exempted so they can concentrate on their work.

manualTranslations.zh: 九曰三長禁姦，不得隔越相領，戶不滿者，隨近并合。
manualTranslations.literal: The ninth said: the three chiefs, in preventing wrongdoing, may not cross boundaries to command one another; where households are insufficient, they should be merged with nearby units.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Ninth: the three chiefs, in suppressing crime, should not command across boundaries; where there are too few households, they should be merged with nearby units.

manualTranslations.zh: 十曰羽林虎賁，邊方有事，暫可赴戰，常戍宜遣蕃兵代之。
manualTranslations.literal: The tenth said: the Yulin and Huben guards may temporarily go to war when there are affairs on the frontier, but for regular garrison duty tribal troops should be sent to replace them.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Tenth: the Yulin and Huben guards may be sent temporarily to fight when there is trouble on the frontier, but regular garrison duty should be assigned to tribal troops in their place.

manualTranslations.zh: 靈太后下其奏，百僚議之，事有同否。
manualTranslations.literal: Empress Dowager Ling sent down his memorial for the hundred officials to discuss, and in the matters there were agreements and disagreements.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Ling sent his memorial down for discussion by the officials, who agreed on some points and disagreed on others.

manualTranslations.zh: 時四中郎將兵數寡弱，不足以襟帶京師，澄奏宜以東中帶滎陽郡，南中帶魯陽郡，西中帶恒農郡，北中帶河內郡，選二品、三品親賢兼稱者居之，省非急之作，配以強兵，如此則深根固本、強幹弱枝之義也。
manualTranslations.literal: At the time the troops of the four Gentlemen Generals of the Center were few and weak, insufficient to belt and protect the capital. Cheng memorialized that the Eastern Center should take in Yingyang Commandery, the Southern Center Luyang Commandery, the Western Center Hengnong Commandery, and the Northern Center Henei Commandery; that men of the second and third ranks who were close, worthy, and qualified should be selected to occupy them; that nonurgent works should be eliminated; and that strong troops should be assigned. In this way, he said, lay the meaning of deepening the roots and strengthening the foundation, strengthening the trunk and weakening the branches.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: At the time the four Central Gentleman-General commands had too few weak troops to protect the capital. Cheng proposed that the Eastern Center be linked with Yingyang Commandery, the Southern Center with Luyang, the Western Center with Hengnong, and the Northern Center with Henei; that qualified close and worthy men of the second and third ranks be chosen to hold them; that nonurgent works be reduced; and that strong troops be assigned. This, he said, would deepen the roots, strengthen the base, strengthen the trunk, and weaken the branches.

manualTranslations.zh: 靈太后初將從之，後議者不同，乃止。
manualTranslations.literal: Empress Dowager Ling at first was about to follow this, but later the discussants disagreed, and so it was stopped.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Ling initially intended to follow the proposal, but later the discussants disagreed, so it was dropped.

manualTranslations.zh: 澄又重奏曰：「固本宜強，防微在豫，故雖有文事，不忘武功。
manualTranslations.literal: Cheng again memorialized, "To secure the root it should be strengthened, and prevention of the slight lies in preparation; therefore, even when there are civil affairs, military achievement is not forgotten.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Cheng memorialized again, "To secure the root, it must be strengthened; to guard against small dangers, one must prepare in advance. Thus even in civil affairs, military power is not forgotten.

manualTranslations.zh: 況今南蠻仍獷，北妖頻結，來事難圖，勢同往變。
manualTranslations.literal: How much more now, when the southern Man remain fierce and the northern demons repeatedly form alliances; future events are difficult to plan for, and the situation is the same as past disturbances.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: How much more now, when the southern Man remain fierce and northern enemies repeatedly combine. Future events are hard to foresee, and the situation resembles past upheavals.

manualTranslations.zh: 脫暴勃忽起，振動關畿，四府羸卒，何以防擬。
manualTranslations.literal: If sudden violence abruptly arises and shakes the passes and capital region, with the weak soldiers of the four offices, how will we defend and prepare?
manualTranslations.idiomatic: If a sudden uprising breaks out and shakes the passes and capital region, how can the weak troops of the four offices defend against it?

manualTranslations.zh: 平康之世，可以寄安，遺之久長，恐非善策。
manualTranslations.literal: In an age of peace and health, we may entrust ourselves to security, but to leave it so for a long time, I fear, is not a good plan.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In peaceful times one may rely on security, but to leave matters this way for long is not good policy.

manualTranslations.zh: 如臣愚見，郎將領兵，兼總民職，省官實祿，於是乎在。
manualTranslations.literal: In my foolish view, that the Gentleman Generals command troops while also overseeing civil duties, and that offices be reduced while real salaries remain, lies precisely here.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In my foolish view, the Gentleman Generals should command troops while also overseeing civil duties; this is where offices can be reduced while real salaries are preserved.

manualTranslations.zh: 求還依前增兵益號，將位既重，則念報亦深，軍郡相依，則表裏俱濟，朝廷無四顧之憂，姦宄絕窺覦之望矣。」
manualTranslations.literal: I ask that we return to the former system of increasing troops and augmenting titles. Once the generals' positions are weighty, their thought of repaying the state will also be deep; when army and commandery rely on each other, inside and outside will both be aided, the court will have no worries on four sides, and criminals will lose any hope of peering in."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: I ask that we return to the earlier plan of increasing troops and strengthening the titles. If the generals' posts are weighty, their sense of obligation will deepen; if army and commandery depend on one another, inner and outer defenses will both be supplied. The court will have no worries on any side, and criminals will lose hope of taking advantage."

manualTranslations.zh: 卒不納。
manualTranslations.literal: In the end it was not accepted.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the end the proposal was not accepted.

manualTranslations.zh: 又以流人初至遠鎮，衣食無資，多有死者，奏并其妻子給糧一歲，從之。
manualTranslations.literal: He also, because exiles newly arrived at distant garrisons had no resources for clothing and food and many died, memorialized that they, together with their wives and children, be given grain for one year, and this was followed.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He also noted that exiles newly sent to distant garrisons lacked clothing and food and often died, so he memorialized that they and their families be given a year's grain. This was approved.

manualTranslations.zh: 尋以疾患，求解任，不許。
manualTranslations.literal: Soon, because of illness, he requested to be relieved of office, but it was not permitted.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he asked to be relieved because of illness, but this was not allowed.

manualTranslations.zh: 蕭衍於浮山斷淮為堰，以灌壽春，乃除使持節、大將軍、大都督、南討諸軍事，勒眾十萬，將出彭宋，尋淮堰自壞，不行。
manualTranslations.literal: When Xiao Yan, at Fushan, cut off the Huai to make a dam in order to flood Shouchun, Cheng was appointed Bearer of the Staff, Grand General, Grand Commander of all armies for the southern campaign, and ordered to command one hundred thousand men and prepare to go out through Peng and Song. Soon the Huai dam broke by itself, and he did not proceed.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Xiao Yan dammed the Huai at Fushan to flood Shouchun, Cheng was appointed Bearer of the Staff, Grand General, and Grand Commander of the southern campaign armies, with orders to lead one hundred thousand men out through Peng and Song. Soon the Huai dam collapsed on its own, and the campaign did not proceed.

manualTranslations.zh: 澄以北邊鎮將選舉彌輕，恐賊虜闚邊，山陵危迫，奏求重鎮將之選，修警備之嚴，詔不從。
manualTranslations.literal: Because Cheng considered the selection of commanders for the northern frontier garrisons increasingly slight, and feared that rebel captives would peer at the border and the imperial tombs would be endangered, he memorialized requesting that selection of garrison commanders be made weightier and the strictness of warning and defense be repaired, but the edict did not follow it.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Cheng believed that commanders for the northern frontier garrisons were being chosen too lightly. Fearing that raiders would threaten the border and endanger the imperial tombs, he memorialized asking that garrison commanders be selected more carefully and defenses tightened, but the edict did not accept this.

manualTranslations.zh: 賊虜入寇，至於舊都，鎮將多非其人，所在叛亂，犯逼山陵，如澄所慮。
manualTranslations.literal: When rebel captives entered and raided, reaching the old capital, many garrison commanders were not the right men, rebellions broke out everywhere, and they violated and pressed upon the imperial tombs, just as Cheng had feared.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When the raiders entered and reached the old capital, many garrison commanders proved unfit, rebellions broke out in many places, and the imperial tombs were threatened, exactly as Cheng had feared.

manualTranslations.zh: 澄奏都城府寺猶未周悉，今軍旅初寧，無宜發眾，請取諸職人及司州郡縣犯十杖已上百鞭已下收贖之物，絹一匹，輸磚二百，以漸修造。
manualTranslations.literal: Cheng memorialized that the offices and temples of the capital city were still not complete; now that military affairs had just become quiet, it was not fitting to mobilize the masses. He requested that they take from various office workers and from the ransom goods paid for offenses in Sizhou commanderies and counties punishable by ten strokes or more and one hundred lashes or less: for one bolt of silk, two hundred bricks should be delivered, gradually to carry out construction.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Cheng memorialized that the capital's offices and temples were still incomplete, but since the armies had only just settled, the people should not be mobilized. He asked instead to use office laborers and the redemption payments for offenses in Sizhou commanderies and counties punishable by ten strokes to one hundred lashes: each bolt of silk would be commuted to two hundred bricks, so construction could proceed gradually.

manualTranslations.zh: 詔從之。
manualTranslations.literal: The edict followed it.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The edict approved this.

manualTranslations.zh: 太傅、清河王懌表奏其事，遂寢不行。
manualTranslations.literal: Grand Tutor Yi, Prince of Qinghe, memorialized on the matter, and it was then set aside and not carried out.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Grand Tutor Yuan Yi, Prince of Qinghe, submitted a memorial about the matter, and it was shelved without being carried out.

manualTranslations.zh: 澄又奏曰：「臣聞賞必以道，用防淫人之姦；
manualTranslations.literal: Cheng again memorialized, "I have heard that rewards must accord with the Way, to guard against the wickedness of excessive men;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Cheng also memorialized, "I have heard that rewards must follow the Way, to guard against the schemes of corrupt men;

manualTranslations.zh: 罰不濫及，以戒良士之困。
manualTranslations.literal: punishments must not reach indiscriminately, in order to warn against the distress of good men.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: punishments must not be indiscriminate, lest good men be driven into distress.

manualTranslations.zh: 刑者，侀也。
manualTranslations.literal: Punishment means modeling.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Punishment is a matter of setting a model.

manualTranslations.zh: 每垂三宥，秉律執請，不得已而用之。
manualTranslations.literal: One always extends the three pardons, and only when holding the law and presenting the request leaves no alternative is it used.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: One should always extend the three pardons, and only when the law is upheld and the request cannot be granted should punishment be used.

manualTranslations.zh: 是故小大之獄，察之以情，一人呼嗟，或虧王道。
manualTranslations.literal: Therefore, in prisons small and great, cases are examined according to feeling; if one person cries out in sorrow, it may diminish the kingly Way.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Thus in cases great and small, one examines the circumstances; even one person crying out in grievance can diminish the kingly Way.

manualTranslations.zh: 刑罰得失，乃興廢之所由也。
manualTranslations.literal: The success and failure of punishments are the route by which states rise or fall.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The success or failure of punishments is the source of a state's rise or decline.

manualTranslations.zh: 竊聞司州牧、高陽王臣雍栲殺奉朝請韓元昭、前門下錄事姚敬賢，雖因公事，理實未盡。
manualTranslations.literal: I have privately heard that Yong, Minister of Sizhou and Prince of Gaoyang, tortured and killed Han Yuanzhao, Gentleman for Court Audience, and Yao Jingxian, former Recorder of the Chancellery. Although this arose from official business, in principle the facts were not exhausted.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: I have heard privately that Yuan Yong, Minister of Sizhou and Prince of Gaoyang, tortured and killed Han Yuanzhao, Gentleman for Court Audience, and Yao Jingxian, former Recorder of the Chancellery. Although this arose from official business, the facts were not fully investigated.

manualTranslations.zh: 何者？
manualTranslations.literal: Why is this?
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Why do I say this?

manualTranslations.zh: 太平之世，草不橫伐，行葦之感，事驗隆周。
manualTranslations.literal: In an age of great peace, even grass is not cut sideways; the feeling of "walking among the reeds" was verified in the flourishing Zhou.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In an age of great peace, even grasses are not wantonly cut; the compassion shown in "Walking among the Reeds" was proven in the flourishing Zhou.

manualTranslations.zh: 若昭等狀彰，死罪以定，應刑於都市，與眾棄之；
manualTranslations.literal: If the circumstances of Zhao and the others were manifest and the capital crime fixed, they should have been executed in the marketplace and cast away with the crowd;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: If the crimes of Yuanzhao and the others were clear and death sentences certain, they should have been executed in the marketplace and cast out before the crowd;

manualTranslations.zh: 如其疑似不分，情理未究，不宜以三清九流之官杖下便死，輕絕民命，傷理敗法。
manualTranslations.literal: if suspicion and likeness were not distinguished and the facts and principle not fully examined, it was not fitting for officials of pure rank and regular service to die beneath the staff, lightly cutting off the people's lives and injuring principle and ruining law.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: if the suspicions had not been distinguished and the facts had not been fully examined, officials of their rank should not have died under the cudgel, their lives lightly cut off in a way that injured principle and ruined law.

manualTranslations.zh: 往年州於大市鞭殺五人，及檢贓狀，全無寸尺。
manualTranslations.literal: In a previous year, the province flogged five men to death in the great marketplace, and when the circumstances of stolen goods were inspected, there was not even an inch or foot of evidence.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In a previous year the province flogged five men to death in the great marketplace, and when the alleged stolen goods were investigated there was not the slightest evidence.

manualTranslations.zh: 今復酷害，一至於此。
manualTranslations.literal: Now again cruel harm has once reached this point.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Now its cruelty has once again gone this far.

manualTranslations.zh: 朝野云云，咸懷驚愕。
manualTranslations.literal: Court and countryside are full of talk, and all harbor shock and alarm.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Court and countryside are talking, and everyone is shocked.

manualTranslations.zh: 若殺生在下，虐專於臣，人君之權，安所復用。
manualTranslations.literal: If killing and giving life are in those below, and cruelty is monopolized by ministers, where can the ruler's authority be used again?
manualTranslations.idiomatic: If life and death lie in the hands of subordinates and cruelty is monopolized by ministers, what use remains for the ruler's authority?

manualTranslations.zh: 自開古以來，明明之世，未聞斯比也。
manualTranslations.literal: From the opening of antiquity onward, in clear and enlightened ages, I have never heard of anything like this.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Since antiquity began, in bright and enlightened ages, I have never heard of such a thing.

manualTranslations.zh: 武王曰：『吾不以一人之命而易天下。』
manualTranslations.literal: King Wu said, "I would not exchange all under Heaven for the life of one man."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: King Wu said, "I would not trade one man's life for all under Heaven."

manualTranslations.zh: 蓋重民命也。
manualTranslations.literal: This was because he valued the people's lives.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: This was because he valued human life.

manualTranslations.zh: 請以見事付廷尉推究，驗其為劫之狀，察其栲殺之理，使是非分明，幽魂獲雪。」
manualTranslations.literal: I request that the present matter be given to the Chamberlain for Law Enforcement for investigation, to verify the circumstances of their robbery and examine the principle of the torture-killings, so that right and wrong may be made clear and the hidden souls may obtain exoneration."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: I request that the case be given to the Chamberlain for Law Enforcement to investigate, verify the alleged robbery, and examine the grounds for the torture-killings, so that right and wrong become clear and the dead may be vindicated."

manualTranslations.zh: 詔從之。
manualTranslations.literal: The edict followed this.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The edict approved this.

manualTranslations.zh: 澄當官而行，無所回避。
manualTranslations.literal: Cheng acted according to his office and had nothing from which he turned aside or avoided.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Cheng acted according to his office and avoided nothing.

manualTranslations.zh: 又奏墾田授受之制八條，甚有綱貫，大便於時。
manualTranslations.literal: He also memorialized eight articles on the system for granting and receiving cultivated fields; they had much order and coherence and were greatly convenient at the time.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He also memorialized eight provisions on the system for allotting reclaimed fields. They were orderly and coherent, and greatly suited the needs of the time.

manualTranslations.zh: 前來尚書文簿，諸曹須，則出借。
manualTranslations.literal: Previously, when documents and registers of the Department of State Affairs were needed by the various bureaus, they were lent out.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Previously, when the various bureaus needed documents and registers from the Department of State Affairs, the records were lent out.

manualTranslations.zh: 時公車署以理冤事重。
manualTranslations.literal: At the time, the Office of Public Carriages considered the handling of grievance cases important.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: At the time, the Office of Public Carriages regarded the handling of grievance cases as important.

manualTranslations.zh: 奏請真案。
manualTranslations.literal: It memorialized requesting the original case files.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: It memorialized requesting the original case files.

manualTranslations.zh: 澄執奏以尚書政本，特宜遠慎，故凡所奏事，閣道通之，蓋以祕要之切，防其宣露，寧有古制所重，今反輕之，內猶設禁，外更寬也。
manualTranslations.literal: Cheng firmly memorialized that the Department of State Affairs was the root of government and especially should be treated with far-reaching caution; therefore, all memorialized affairs were transmitted through the gallery passage, precisely because of the urgent importance of secrecy and to guard against their being disclosed. How could something valued by the ancient system now instead be treated lightly, with prohibitions still set inside while outside they were made even looser?
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Cheng insisted in a memorial that the Department of State Affairs was the root of government and had to be handled with special caution. All memorialized matters were transmitted through the palace galleries precisely because secrecy was urgent and disclosure had to be prevented. How could something the ancient system treated as weighty now be treated lightly, keeping restrictions inside while loosening them outside?

manualTranslations.zh: 宜繕寫事意，以付公車。
manualTranslations.literal: The meaning of the matter should be copied out and given to the Office of Public Carriages.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The substance of the case should be copied out and given to the Office of Public Carriages.

任城王雲，年五歲，恭宗崩，號哭不絕聲。世祖聞之而呼，抱之泣曰：「汝何知而有成人之意也！」和平五年封，拜使持節、侍中、征東大將軍、和龍鎮都大將。顯祖時，拜都督中外諸軍事、中都坐大官，聽理民訟，甚收時譽。延興中，顯祖集羣僚，欲禪位於京兆王子推。王公卿士，莫敢先言。雲進曰：「陛下方隆太平，臨覆四海，豈得上違宗廟，下棄兆民。父子相傳，其來久矣，皇魏之興，未之有革。皇儲正統，聖德夙章。陛下必欲割捐塵務，頤神清曠者，冢副之寄，宜紹寶曆，若欲捨儲，輕移宸極，恐非先聖之意，駭動人情。又，天下是祖宗之天下，而陛下輒改神器，上乖七廟七靈，下長姦亂之道，此是禍福所由，願深思慎之。」太尉源賀又進曰：「陛下今欲外選諸王而禪位于皇叔者，臣恐春秋蒸嘗，昭穆有亂，脫萬世之後，必有逆饗之譏，深願思任城之言。」東陽公元丕等進曰：「皇太子雖聖德夙彰，然實沖幼。陛下富於春秋，始覽機政，普天景仰，率土傒心，欲隆獨善，不以萬物為意，其若宗廟何，其若億兆何！」顯祖曰：「儲宮正統，受終文祖，羣公相之，有何不可。」於是傳位於高祖。後蠕蠕犯塞，雲為中軍大都督，從顯祖討之，遇於大磧。事具蠕蠕傳。後仇池氐反，以雲為征西大將軍討平之。除都督徐兗二州緣淮諸軍事、征東大將軍、開府、徐州刺史。雲以太妃蓋氏薨，表求解任，顯祖不許，雲悲號動疾，乃許之。性善撫綏，得徐方之心，為百姓所追戀。送遺錢貨，一無所受。顯祖聞而嘉之。復拜侍中、中都大官，賜帛千匹、羊千口。出為冀州刺史，仍本將軍。雲留心政事，甚得下情，於是合州請戶輸絹五尺、粟五升以報雲恩。高祖嘉之，遷使持節、都督陝西諸軍事、征南大將軍、長安鎮都大將、雍州刺史。雲廉謹自修，留心庶獄，挫抑豪強，羣盜息止，州民頌之者千有餘人。文明太后嘉之，賜帛千匹。太和五年，薨於州。遺令薄葬，勿受賵禭。諸子奉遵其旨。喪至京師，車駕親臨，哭之哀慟，贈以本官，諡曰康。陪葬雲中之金陵。雲長子澄，字道鎮，少而好學。及康王薨，澄居喪以孝聞。襲封，加征北大將軍。高祖時，蠕蠕犯塞，加澄使持節、都督北討諸軍事以討之。蠕蠕遁走，又以氐羌反叛，除都督梁益荊三州諸軍事、征南大將軍、梁州刺史。文明太后引見澄，誡厲之，顧謂中書令李沖曰：「此兒風神吐發，德音閑婉，當為宗室領袖。是行使之必稱我意。卿但記之，我不妄談人物也。」梁州氐帥楊仲顯、婆羅、楊卜兄弟及符叱盤等，自以居邊地險，世為山狡。澄至州，量彼風俗，誘導懷附。表送婆羅，授仲顯循城鎮副將，楊卜廣業太守，叱盤固道鎮副將，自餘首帥，各隨才而用之，款附者賞，違命加誅，於是仇池帖然，西南款順。加侍中，賜衣一襲、乘馬一匹，以旌其能。後轉征東大將軍、開府、徐州刺史，甚有聲績。朝於京師，引見於皇信堂。高祖詔澄曰：「昔鄭子產鑄刑書，而晉叔向非之。此二人皆是賢士，得失竟誰？」對曰：「鄭國寡弱，攝於強鄰，民情去就，非刑莫制，故鑄刑書以示威。雖乖古式，合今權道，隨時濟世，子產為得。而叔向譏議，示不忘古，可與論道，未可語權。」高祖曰：「任城當欲為魏之子產也。」澄曰：「子產道合當時，聲流竹素。臣既庸近，何敢庶幾。今陛下以四海為家，宣文德以懷天下，但江外尚阻，車書未一，季世之民，易以威伏，難以禮治。愚謂子產之法，猶應暫用，大同之後，便以道化之。」高祖心方革變，深善其對，笑曰：「非任城無以識變化之體。朕方創改朝制，當與任城共萬世之功耳。」後徵為中書令，改授尚書令。蕭賾使庾蓽來朝，蓽見澄音韻遒雅，風儀秀逸，謂主客郎張彝曰：「往魏任城以武著稱，今魏任城乃以文見美也。」時詔延四廟之子，下逮玄孫之冑，申宗宴於皇信堂，不以爵秩為列，悉序昭穆為次，用家人之禮。高祖曰：「行禮已畢，欲令宗室各言其志，可率賦詩。」特令澄為七言連韻，與高祖往復賭賽，遂至極歡，際夜乃罷。後高祖外示南討，意在謀遷，齋於明堂左个，詔太常卿王諶，親令龜卜，易筮南伐之事，其兆遇革。高祖曰：「此是湯武革命，順天應人之卦也。」羣臣莫敢言。澄進曰：「易言革者更也。將欲應天順人，革君臣之命，湯武得之為吉。階下帝有天下，重光累葉。今曰卜征，乃可伐叛，不得云革命。此非君人之卦，未可全為吉也。」高祖厲聲曰：「象云『大人虎變』，何言不吉也！」澄曰：「陛下龍興既久，豈可方同虎變！」高祖勃然作色曰：「社稷我社稷，任城而欲沮眾也！」澄曰：「社稷誠知陛下之社稷，然臣是社稷之臣子，豫參顧問，敢盡愚衷。」高祖既銳意必行，惡澄此對，久之乃解，曰：「各言其志，亦復何傷。」車駕還宮，便召澄，未及昇階，遙謂曰：「向者之革卦，今更欲論之。明堂之忿，懼眾人競言，阻我大計，故厲色怖文武耳，想解朕意也。」乃獨謂澄曰：「今日之行，誠知不易。但國家興自北土，徙居平城，雖富有四海，文軌未一，此間用武之地，非可文治，移風易俗，信為甚難。崤函帝宅，河洛王里，因茲大舉，光宅中原，任城意以為何如？」澄曰：「伊洛中區，均天下所據，陛下制御華夏，輯平九服，蒼生聞此，應當大慶。」高祖曰：「北人戀本，忽聞將移，不能不驚擾也。」澄曰：「此既非常之事，當非常人所知，唯須決之聖懷，此輩亦何能為也。」高祖曰：「任城便是我之子房。」加撫軍大將軍、太子少保，又兼尚書左僕射。及駕幸洛陽，定遷都之策，高祖詔曰：「遷移之旨，必須訪眾。當遣任城馳驛向代，問彼百司，論擇可否。近日論革，今真所謂革也，王其勉之。」既至代都，眾聞遷詔，莫不驚駭。澄援引今古，徐以曉之，眾乃開伏。澄遂南馳還報，會車駕於滑臺。高祖大悅曰：「若非任城，朕事業不得就也。」從幸鄴宮，除吏部尚書。及幸代，車駕北巡，留澄銓簡舊臣。初，魏自公侯以下，迄于選臣，動有萬數，冗散無事。澄品為三等，量其優劣，盡其能否之用，咸無怨者。駕還洛京，復兼右僕射。高祖至北邙，遂幸洪池，命澄侍昇龍舟，因賦詩以序懷。高祖曰：「朕昨夜夢一老公，頭鬢皓白，正理冠服，拜立路左。朕怪而問之，自云晉侍中嵇紹，故此奉迎。神爽卑懼，似有求焉。」澄對曰：「晉世之亂，嵇紹以身衞主，殞命御側，亦是晉之忠臣；比干遭紂兇虐，忠諫剖心，可謂殷之良士。二人俱死於王事，墳塋並在於道周。然陛下徙御經殷墟而弔比干，至洛陽而遺嵇紹，當是希恩而感夢。」高祖曰：「朕何德，能幽感達士也。然實思追禮先賢，標揚忠懿，比干、嵇紹皆是古之誠烈，而朕務濃於比干，禮略於嵇紹，情有愧然。既有此夢，或如任城所言。」於是求其兆域，遣使弔祭焉。蕭鸞既殺蕭昭業而自立，昭業雍州刺史曹虎請以襄陽內附。分遣諸將，車駕將自赴之。豫州又表，虎奉誠之使不復重來。高祖引澄及咸陽王禧、彭城王勰、司徒馮誕、司空穆亮、鎮南李沖等議之。高祖曰：「比得邊州表云，襄陽慕化，朕將鳴鑾江沔，為彼聲勢。今復表稱，更無後信，於行留之計，竟欲如何？」禧等或云宜行，或言宜止。高祖曰：「眾人紛紜，意見不等，朕莫知所從。必欲盡行留之勢，使言理俱暢者，宜有客主，共相起發。任城與鎮南為應留之議，朕當為宜行之論，諸公俱坐聽得失，長者從之。」於是高祖曰：「二賢試言留計也。」沖對曰：「臣等正以徒御草創，人斯樂安，內而應者未審，不宜輕爾動發。」高祖曰：「襄陽款問，似當是虛。亦知初遷之民，無宜勞役。脫歸誠有實，即當乘其悅附，遠則有會稽之會，近則略平江北。如其送款是虛，且可遊巡淮楚，問民之瘼，使彼土蒼生，知君德之所在，復何所損而惜此一舉？脫降問是實，而停不撫接，不亦稽阻款誠，毀朕大略也。」澄曰：「降問若審，應有表質。而使人一返，靜無音問，其詐也可見。今代遷之眾，人懷戀本，細累相攜，始就洛邑，居無一椽之室，家闕儋石之糧，而使怨苦即戎，泣當白刃，恐非歌舞之師也。今茲區宇初構，又東作方興，正是子來百堵之日，農夫肆力之秋，宜寬彼逋誅，惠此民庶。且三軍已援，無稽赴接。苟其款實，力足納撫，待克平襄沔，然後動駕。今無故勞涉，空為往返，恐挫損天威，更成賊膽，願上覽盤庚始遷之艱難，下矜詩人由庚之至詠，輯寧新邑，惠康億兆。」而司空亮以為宜行，公卿皆同之。澄謂亮曰：「公在外見旌鉞既張，而有憂色，每聞談論，不願此行，何得對聖顏更如斯之語也。面背不同，事涉欺佞，非所謂論道之德，更失國士之體，或有傾側，當由公輩佞臣。」李沖曰：「任城王可謂忠於社稷，願陛下深察其言。臣等在外，皆憚征行，唯貴與賤，不謀同辭，仰願聖心裁其可否。」高祖曰：「任城適以公等從朕，有如此論。不從朕者，何必皆忠而通識安危也。小忠是大忠之賊，無乃似諸？」澄曰：「臣既愚闇，不識大理，所可言者，雖涉小忠，要是竭盡微款，不知大忠者竟何據？」高祖曰：「任城脫居台鼎之任，欲令大忠在己也。」澄曰：「臣誠才非台弼，智闕和鼎，脫得濫居公鉉，庶當官而行，不負愚志。」高祖大笑。澄又謂亮曰：「昔汲黯於漢武前面折公孫食脫粟飯，臥布被，云其詐也。于時公孫謙讓下之。武帝歎汲黯至忠，公孫長者，二人稱賢。公既道均昔士，願思長者之言。」高祖笑曰：「任城欲自比汲黯也。且所言是公，未知得失所在，何便謝司空也。」駕遂南伐。五等開建，食邑一千戶。後從征至懸瓠，以篤疾還京。駕餞之汝濆，賦詩而別。車駕還洛，引見王公侍臣於清徽堂。高祖曰：「此堂成來，未與王公行宴樂之禮。後東閤廡堂粗復始就，故今與諸賢欲無高而不昇，無小而不入。」因之流化渠。高祖曰：「此曲水者亦有其義，取乾道曲成，萬物無滯。」次之洗煩池。高祖曰：「此池中亦有嘉魚。」澄曰：「此所謂『魚在在藻，有頒其首』。」高祖曰：「且取『王在靈沼，於牣魚躍』。」次之觀德殿。高祖曰：「射以觀德，故遂命之。」次之凝閑堂。高祖曰：「名目要有其義，此蓋取夫子閑居之義。不可縱奢以忘儉，自安以忘危，故此堂後作茅茨堂。」謂李沖曰：「此東曰步元廡，西曰遊凱廡。此堂雖無唐堯之君，卿等當無愧於元、凱。」沖對曰：「臣既遭唐堯之君，不敢辭元、凱之譽。」高祖曰：「光景垂落，朕同宗則有載考之義，卿等將出無遠，何得默爾，不示德音。」即命黃門侍郎崔光、郭祚，通直郎邢巒、崔休等賦詩言志。燭至，公卿辭退。李沖再拜上千萬歲壽。高祖曰：「卿向以燭至致辭，復獻千萬之壽，朕報卿以南山之詩。」高祖曰：「燭至辭退，庶姓之禮；在夜載考，宗族之義。卿等且還，朕與諸王宗室，欲成此夜飲。」又從幸鄴。還洛，以出納之勞，增邑五百戶。坐公事免官。尋兼吏部尚書。恒州刺史穆泰在州謀反，推朔州刺史陽平王頤為主。頤表其狀。高祖召澄入見凝閑堂，曰：「適得陽平表曰，穆泰謀為不軌，招誘宗室。脫或必然，遷京甫爾，北人戀舊，南北紛擾，朕洛陽不立也。此事非任城不辦，可為我力疾向北。如其弱也，直往擒翦；若其勢強，可承制發并肆兵以殄之。雖知王患，既是國家大事，不容辭也。」澄曰：「泰等愚惑，正戀本為此，非有遠圖。臣誠怯弱，不憚是輩，雖復患惙，豈敢有辭。謹當罄盡心力，繼之以死，願陛下勿憂。」高祖笑曰：「得任城此行，朕復何憂也。」遂授節，銅虎、竹使符，御仗，左右，仍行恒州事。行達雁門，太守夜告泰已握眾西就陽平，城下聚結，唯見弓仗。澄聞便速進。時右丞孟斌曰：「事不可量，須依敕召并肆兵，然後徐動。」澄曰：「泰既構逆，應據堅城，而更迎陽平，度其所為，似當勢弱。泰既不相拒，無故發兵，非宜也。但速往鎮之，民心自定。」遂倍道兼行，出其不意。又遣治書侍御史李煥先赴，至即擒泰，民情怡然。窮其黨與，罪人皆得，鉅鹿公陸叡、安樂侯元隆等百餘人皆獄禁。具狀表聞，高祖覽表大悅，召集公卿以下以表示之，曰：「我任城可謂社稷臣也，尋其罪案，正復臯陶斷獄，豈能過之。」顧謂咸陽王等曰：「汝等脫當其處，不能辦此。」車駕尋幸平城，勞澄曰：「任城此行，深副遠寄。」對曰：「陛下威靈遠被，罪人無所逃刑，臣何勞之有。」引見逆徒，無一人稱枉，時人莫不歎之。高祖顧謂左右曰：「昔仲尼云：『聽訟吾猶人也，必也使無訟乎。』然聖人之聽訟，殆非常人所匹，必也無訟，今日見之矣。」以澄正尚書。車駕南伐，留澄居守，復兼右僕射。澄表請以國秩一歲租布帛助供軍資，詔受其半。高祖幸鄴，值高車樹者反叛，車駕將親討之。澄表諫不宜親行。會江陽王繼平之，乃止。高祖還洛，引見公卿。高祖曰：「營國之本，禮教為先。朕離京邑以來，禮教為日新以不？」澄對曰：「臣謂日新。」高祖曰：「朕昨入城，見車上婦人冠帽而著小襦襖者，若為如此，尚書何為不察？」澄曰：「著猶少於不著者。」高祖曰：「深可怪也！任城意欲令全著乎？一言可以喪邦者，斯之謂歟？可命史官書之。」又曰：「王者不降佐於蒼昊，皆拔才而用之。朕失於舉人，任許一羣婦人輩奇事，當更銓簡耳。任城在省，為舉天下綱維，為當署事而已？」澄曰：「臣實署事而已。」高祖曰：「如此便一令史足矣，何待任城。」又曰：「我遣舍人宣詔，何為使小人聞之？」澄曰：「時雖有幹吏，去榜亦遠。」高祖曰：「遠則不聞，聞則不遠。既得聞詔，理故可知。」於是留守羣臣遂免冠謝罪。尋除尚書右僕射。蕭寶卷遣其太尉陳顯達入寇漢陽。是時高祖不豫，引澄入見清徽堂。詔曰：「顯達侵亂，沔陽不安，朕不親行，莫攘此賊。朕疾患淹年，氣力惙弊，如有非常，委任城大事。是段任城必須從朕。」澄涕泣對曰：「臣謹當竭股肱之力，以命上報。」遂從駕南伐。高祖崩，澄受顧命。世宗初，有降人嚴叔懋告尚書令王肅遣孔思達潛通寶卷，圖為叛逆，寶卷遣俞公喜送敕於肅，公喜還南，肅與裴叔業馬為信。澄信之，乃表肅將叛，輒下禁止。咸陽、北海二王奏澄擅禁宰輔，免官歸第。尋出為平西將軍、梁州刺史。辭以母老。除安東將軍、相州刺史，復固辭。改授安西將軍、雍州刺史。尋徵赴季秋講武。除都督淮南諸軍事、鎮南大將軍、開府、揚州刺史。下車封孫叔敖之墓，毀蔣子文之廟。頻表南伐，世宗不許。又辭母老，乞解州任，寢而不報。加散騎常侍。澄表曰：「臣參訓先朝，藉規有日，前言舊軌，頗亦聞之。又昔在恒代，親習皇宗，熟祕序疑庭無闕日。臣每於侍坐，先帝未嘗不以書典在懷，禮經為事，周旋之則，不輟於時。自鳳舉中京，方隆禮教，宗室之範，每蒙委及，四門之選，負荷銓量。自先皇升遐，未遑修述，學宮虛荷四門之名，宗人有闕四時之業，青衿之緒，於茲將廢。臣每惟其事，竊所傷懷。伏惟聖略宏遠，四方罕務，宴安之辰，於是乎在。何為太平之世，而令子衿之歎興焉；聖明之日，而使宗人之訓闕焉。愚謂可敕有司，修復皇宗之學，開闢四門之教，使將落之族，日就月將。」詔曰：「冑子崇業，自古盛典，國均之訓，無應久廢，尚書更可量宜修立。」澄又表母疾解州任，不聽。蕭衍將張囂之寇陷夷陵戍，澄遣輔國將軍成興步騎赴討，大破之，復夷陵，囂之遁走。又遣長風戍主奇道顯攻蕭衍陰山戍，破之，斬其戍主龍驤將軍、都亭侯梅興祖。仍引攻白槀戍，又破之，斬其寧朔將軍、關內侯吳道爽。澄表曰：「蕭衍頻斷東關，欲令巢湖汎溢。湖周回四百餘里，東關合江之際，廣不過數十步，若賊計得成，大湖傾注者，則淮南諸戍必同晉陽之事矣。又吳楚便水，且灌且掠，淮南之地，將非國有。壽陽去江五百餘里，眾庶惶惶，並懼水害。脫乘民之願，攻敵之虛，豫勒諸州，纂集士馬，首秋大集，則南瀆可為飲馬之津，霍嶺必成徙倚之觀，事貴應機，經略須早。縱混一不可必果，江西自是無虞。若猶豫緩圖，不加除討，關塞既成，襄陵方及，平原民戍定為魚矣。」詔發冀、定、瀛、相、并、濟六州二萬人，馬一千五百匹，令仲秋之中畢會淮南，并壽陽先兵三萬，委澄經略。先是朝議有南伐之意，以蕭寶夤為東揚州刺史據東城，陳伯之為江州刺史戍陽石，以澄總督二鎮，授之節度。至是勒兵進討。以東關水衝，大峴險要，東關縱水，陽石、合肥有急懸之切，不圖大峴，則歷陽有乘險之援，淮陵陸道，九山水路，並宜經略。於是遣統軍傅豎眼、王神念等進次大峴、東關、九山、淮陵，皆分部諸將，倍道據之，總勒大眾，絡繹相接。而神念克其關要、潁川二城，斬衍軍主費尼。而寧朔將軍韋惠、龍驤將軍李伯由仍固大峴。澄遣統軍党法宗、傅豎眼等進軍克之，遂圍白塔、牽城，數日之間，便即逃潰。衍清溪戍望風散走。衍徐州刺史司馬明素率眾三千，欲援九山；徐州長史潘伯隣規固淮陵；寧朔將軍王燮負險焦城。法宗進克焦城，破淮陵，擒明素，斬伯隣。其濟陰太守王厚強、廬江太守裴邃即亦奔退。詔澄曰：「將軍文德內昭，武功外暢，奮揚大略，將蕩江吳。長旌始舒，賊徒懾氣，銳旅方馳，東關席卷。想江湖弭波，在旦夕耳。所送首虜，並已聞之。」初，澄出討之後，衍將姜慶真襲據壽春外郭，齊王蕭寶夤擊走之。長史韋纘坐免官，澄以在外無坐。遂攻鍾離。又詔：「鍾離若食盡，三月已前，固有可克，如至四月，淮水泛長，舟行無礙，宜善量之。前事捷也，此實將軍經略，勳有常焉。如或以水盛難圖，亦可為萬全之計，不宜昧利無成，以貽後悔也。」蕭衍冠軍將軍張惠紹，游擊將軍殷暹、驍騎將軍趙景悅、龍驤將軍張景仁等率眾五千，送糧鍾離。澄遣統軍王足、劉思祖等邀擊惠紹等，大破之。獲惠紹、殷暹、景仁及其屯騎校尉史文淵等軍主以上二十七人。既而遇雨，淮水暴長，引歸壽春。還既狼狽，失兵四千餘人。頻表解州，世宗不許。有司奏軍還失路，奪其開府，又降三階。時蕭衍有移，求換張惠紹。澄表請不許，詔付八座會議。尚書令、廣陽王嘉等奏宜還之，詔乃聽還。後果復寇邊。轉澄鎮北大將軍、定州刺史。初，民中每有橫調，百姓煩苦，前後牧守，未能蠲除，澄多所省減，民以忻賴。又明黜陟賞罰之法，表減公園之地，以給無業貧口，禁造布絹不任衣者。母孟太妃薨，居喪毀瘠，當世稱之。服闋，除太子太保。於時高肇當朝，猜忌賢戚。澄為肇間構，常恐不全，乃終日昏飲，以示荒敗。所作詭越，時謂為狂。世宗夜崩，時事倉卒，高肇擁兵於外，肅宗沖幼，朝野不安。澄疏斥不預機要，而朝望所屬，領軍于忠、侍中崔光等奏澄為尚書令，於是眾心忻服。又加散騎常侍、驃騎大將軍，尋遷司空，加侍中，俄詔領尚書令。初，正始之末，詔百司普昇一級，而執事者不達旨意，刺史、守、令限而不及。澄奏曰：「竊惟雲構鬱起，澤及百司，企春望榮，內外同慶。至於賞陟，不及守宰，爾來十年，冤訟不絕。封回自鎮遠、安州入為太尉長史，元匡自征虜、恒州入作宗卿，二人遷授，並在先詔。應蒙之理，備在於斯。兼州佐停私之徒，陪臣郡丞之例，尚蒙天澤下降，榮及當時。然參佐之來，皆因府主，今府主不霑，佐官獨預，棄本賞末，愚謂未允。今計刺史、守、宰之官，請準回匡，悉同汎限，上允初旨百司之章，下覆訟者元元之心。」詔曰：「自今已後，內外之事，嘗經先朝者，不得重聞。」澄奏曰：「臣聞堯懸諫諍之鼓，舜置誹謗之木，皆所以廣耳目於芻蕘，達四聰於天下。伏惟太祖開基，化隆自遠，累聖相承，於今九帝。重光疊照，汚隆必同，與奪隨時，道無恒體。思過如渴，言重千金，故稱無諱之朝，邁蹤三、五。高祖沖年纂曆，文明協統，變官易律，未為違典。及慈聖臨朝，母儀宇縣，爰發慈令，垂心滯獄，深枉者仰日月於九泉，微屈者希曲照於盆下。今乃格以先朝，限以一例，斯誠奉遵之本心，實乖元元之至望。在于謙挹，有乖舊典。謹尋抱枉求直，或經累朝。毫釐之差，正之宜速；謬若千里，駟馬弗追。故禮有損益，事有可否，父有諍子，君有諫臣，琴瑟不調，理宜改作。是以防川之論，小決則通；鄉校之言，擁則敗國。矧伊陳屈，而可抑以先朝。且先朝屈者，非故屈之，或有司愛憎，或執事濁僻，空文致法，以誤視聽。如此冤塞，彌在可哀。僭之與濫，寧失不經，乞收今旨，還依前詔。」詔曰：「省奏，深體毗贊之情，三皇異軌，五代殊風，一時之制，何必詮改。必謂虛文設旨，理在可申者，何容不同來執。可依往制。」澄表上皇誥宗制并訓詁各一卷，意欲皇太后覽之，思勸戒之益。又奏利國濟民所宜振舉者十條。一曰律度量衡，公私不同，所宜一之。二曰宜興學校，以明黜陟之法。三曰宜興滅繼絕，各舉所知。四曰五調之外，一不煩民，任民之力，不過三日。五曰臨民之官，皆須黜陟，以旌賞罰。六曰逃亡代輸，去來年久者，若非伎作，任聽即住。七曰邊兵逃走，或實陷沒，皆須精檢；三長及近親，若實隱之，徵其代輸，不隱勿論。八曰工商世業之戶，復徵租調，無以堪濟，今請免之，使專其業。九曰三長禁姦，不得隔越相領，戶不滿者，隨近并合。十曰羽林虎賁，邊方有事，暫可赴戰，常戍宜遣蕃兵代之。靈太后下其奏，百僚議之，事有同否。時四中郎將兵數寡弱，不足以襟帶京師，澄奏宜以東中帶滎陽郡，南中帶魯陽郡，西中帶恒農郡，北中帶河內郡，選二品、三品親賢兼稱者居之，省非急之作，配以強兵，如此則深根固本、強幹弱枝之義也。靈太后初將從之，後議者不同，乃止。澄又重奏曰：「固本宜強，防微在豫，故雖有文事，不忘武功。況今南蠻仍獷，北妖頻結，來事難圖，勢同往變。脫暴勃忽起，振動關畿，四府羸卒，何以防擬。平康之世，可以寄安，遺之久長，恐非善策。如臣愚見，郎將領兵，兼總民職，省官實祿，於是乎在。求還依前增兵益號，將位既重，則念報亦深，軍郡相依，則表裏俱濟，朝廷無四顧之憂，姦宄絕窺覦之望矣。」卒不納。又以流人初至遠鎮，衣食無資，多有死者，奏并其妻子給糧一歲，從之。尋以疾患，求解任，不許。蕭衍於浮山斷淮為堰，以灌壽春，乃除使持節、大將軍、大都督、南討諸軍事，勒眾十萬，將出彭宋，尋淮堰自壞，不行。澄以北邊鎮將選舉彌輕，恐賊虜闚邊，山陵危迫，奏求重鎮將之選，修警備之嚴，詔不從。賊虜入寇，至於舊都，鎮將多非其人，所在叛亂，犯逼山陵，如澄所慮。澄奏都城府寺猶未周悉，今軍旅初寧，無宜發眾，請取諸職人及司州郡縣犯十杖已上百鞭已下收贖之物，絹一匹，輸磚二百，以漸修造。詔從之。太傅、清河王懌表奏其事，遂寢不行。澄又奏曰：「臣聞賞必以道，用防淫人之姦；罰不濫及，以戒良士之困。刑者，侀也。每垂三宥，秉律執請，不得已而用之。是故小大之獄，察之以情，一人呼嗟，或虧王道。刑罰得失，乃興廢之所由也。竊聞司州牧、高陽王臣雍栲殺奉朝請韓元昭、前門下錄事姚敬賢，雖因公事，理實未盡。何者？太平之世，草不橫伐，行葦之感，事驗隆周。若昭等狀彰，死罪以定，應刑於都市，與眾棄之；如其疑似不分，情理未究，不宜以三清九流之官杖下便死，輕絕民命，傷理敗法。往年州於大市鞭殺五人，及檢贓狀，全無寸尺。今復酷害，一至於此。朝野云云，咸懷驚愕。若殺生在下，虐專於臣，人君之權，安所復用。自開古以來，明明之世，未聞斯比也。武王曰：『吾不以一人之命而易天下。』蓋重民命也。請以見事付廷尉推究，驗其為劫之狀，察其栲殺之理，使是非分明，幽魂獲雪。」詔從之。澄當官而行，無所回避。又奏墾田授受之制八條，甚有綱貫，大便於時。前來尚書文簿，諸曹須，則出借。時公車署以理冤事重。奏請真案。澄執奏以尚書政本，特宜遠慎，故凡所奏事，閣道通之，蓋以祕要之切，防其宣露，寧有古制所重，今反輕之，內猶設禁，外更寬也。宜繕寫事意，以付公車。

localRange.text: 任城王任城王雲，年五歲，恭宗崩，號哭不絕聲。世祖聞之而呼，抱之泣曰：「汝何知而有成人之意也！和平五年封，拜使持節、侍中、征東大將軍、和龍鎮都大將。顯祖時，拜都督中外諸軍事、中都坐大官，聽理民訟，甚收時譽。延興中，顯祖集羣僚，欲禪位於京兆王子推。王公卿士，莫敢先言。雲進曰：「陛下方隆太平，臨覆四海，豈得上違宗廟，下棄兆民。父子相傳，其來久矣，皇魏之興，未之有革。皇儲正統，聖德夙章。陛下必欲割捐塵務，頤神清曠者，冢副之寄，宜紹寶曆，若欲捨儲，[1]輕移宸極，恐非先聖之意，駭動人情。又，天下是祖宗之天下，而陛下輒改神器，上乖七廟七靈，下長姦亂之道，此是禍福所由，願深思慎之。太尉源賀又進曰：「陛下今欲外選諸王而禪位于皇叔者，臣恐春秋蒸嘗，昭穆有亂，脫萬世之後，必有逆饗之譏，深願思任城之言。東陽公元丕等進曰：「皇太子雖聖德夙彰，然實沖幼。陛下富於春秋，始覽機政，普天景仰，率土傒心，欲隆獨善，不以萬物為意，其若宗廟何，其若億兆何！顯祖曰：「儲宮正統，受終文祖，羣公相之，有何不可。於是傳位於高祖。後蠕蠕犯塞，雲為中軍大都督，從顯祖討之，遇於大磧。事具蠕蠕傳。後仇池氐反，以雲為征西大將軍討平之。除都督徐兗二州緣淮諸軍事、征東大將軍、開府、徐州刺史。雲以太妃蓋氏薨，[2]表求解任，顯南安王城陽王章武王樂陵王安定王1.1.1英子攸1.1.2攸弟中山文莊王熙（附子景獻仲獻叔獻叔仁／叔仁子琳）1.1.3熙弟誘（附子始伯）1.1.4誘弟東平文貞王略（附子景式）1.1.5略弟纂（附子子獻）1.1.6熙異母弟武邑王義興（附子述）1.2.1子魯郡王肅（附子道與）2.2.1子城陽文獻王徽（附子延）2.2.2徽長兄顯魏2.2.3徽次兄顯恭（附子彦昭）2.2.4顯恭弟襄城郡王旭3.1.1長子章武莊武王融（附子景哲、朗、黃頭）3.1.2融弟東安王凝（附子彦友）3.1.3凝弟漁陽王湛（附子俊）3.1.4凝弟晏4.1.1子樂陵惠王景略（附子霸）4.1.2景略弟慶略（附子子政）4.1.3慶略弟洪略4.1.4洪略弟子業5.2.1子超（附子孝景）5.3.1子緒（附子南郡王長春）5.5.1子叔遵南安惠王楨

sourceRange.text: 長子肅，起家員外散騎侍郎，轉直寢。莊帝初，封肅魯郡王，邑千戶。除散騎常侍，出為後將軍、廣州刺史。後除衞將軍、肆州刺史。其弟曄僭立，拜肅侍中、太師、錄尚書事。尋改除使持節、都督青膠光齊南青五州諸軍事、驃騎大將軍、東南道大行臺、青州刺史，不行。永熙二年薨。贈使持節、侍中、都督并恒二州諸軍事、本將軍、司徒公、并州刺史。

localRange.text: 校勘記亦或居安生疾諸本「安」訛「要」。今據冊府卷三八九〈四六二一頁〉改。衍中軍大將軍臨川王蕭宏尚書右僕射柳惔等大將五人沿淮南走諸本「右」作「左」。冊府卷二九０〈三四二０頁〉作「右」。按卷八世宗紀正始三年九月己丑記此事也作「右僕射柳惔」。柳惔為右僕射見梁書卷二武帝紀天監三年正月戊申條及卷一二本傳。「左」字訛，今據改。一一具聞諸本「一一」二字訛作「三」，不可通，局本改作「王」。今據冊府卷四三九〈五二一二頁〉改。遷大將軍尚書令按墓誌集釋元略墓誌〈圖版一三九〉稱「尋遷驃騎大將軍、儀同三司，加國子祭酒，俄涉尚書令」。北魏大將軍在三公上，元略軍號本是車騎大將軍，一般不可能超遷大將軍。這裏「大將軍」上當脫「驃騎」二字。頻為北都大將按「北」下疑脫「鎮」字。統萬鎮都大將朔州刺史張森楷云：「北史〈卷一八〉『朔』作『夏』。據上文「為統萬鎮都大將」，統萬在夏州，不在朔州，疑魏書誤。又刺史例不在所督州之外，上文『都督東秦豳夏三州』，無朔州，尤確證也。按墓誌集釋元彬墓誌〈圖版一四九〉亦作「統萬突鎮都大將、夏州刺史」，張說是。轉尚書左司郎中墓誌集釋元湛墓誌〈圖版一五二〉作「尋補尚書左士郎中」。按晉書卷二四職官志尚書郎條稱西晉時尚書有三十五曹，其中有「左、右士」。又稱東晉所省尚書諸曹中也有「左、右士」。知左、右士曹是西晉舊置。本書卷八一山偉傳〈補〉說山偉「後正名士郎」，「名」字當是「左」或「右」之訛，可證北魏有左、右士郎中。至於「左、右司郎中」，當時並無此官。通典卷二僕射條附有「左、右司郎中」，云：「隋煬帝三年於尚書都省初置左、右司郎二人」，此即隋書卷二八百官志下煬帝所置之「都司郎」。隋於諸曹郎中都去「中」字，故此官初置也只稱左、右司郎，直至唐代始名「左、右司郎中」。隋前不聞有此官。這裏原文當也是「左士郎中」，與墓誌同，後人以「左士」之名罕見，妄改作「左司郎中」。正始四年薨墓誌集釋元思墓誌〈圖版一五五〉「四年」作「三年」。疑傳誤。除持節冠軍將軍幽州刺史按墓誌集釋元彥〈即景略〉墓誌〈圖版一五六〉稱：「延昌之末，遷為持節都督豳州諸軍事、豳州刺史。下云「剋莅西蕃」，與豳州地望相合。這裏「幽」字當是「豳」之訛。改服錫衰諸本「錫」作「裼」，北史百衲本作「錫」。按「錫衰」見禮記喪服小記。「錫」是細布。「裼」乃「錫」之形訛，今據改。後復本封尒朱榮之入洛超避難洛南遇寇見害按卷一０莊帝紀武泰元年四月庚子記河陰被殺諸王有「北平王超」，是月甲辰記「以北平王超還復為安定王」。傳稱生前已復本封，疑誤。至於紀以超死於河陰之禍，傳稱「遇寇見害」，亦不合。願平弟永平征虜將軍南州刺史按地形志無「南州」。北周於今四川萬縣置南州、南都郡、源陽縣，事在後，見隋書卷二九地理志上巴東郡武寧縣條。這裏「南」下當脫一字。

manualTranslations.zh: 蕭寶卷遣將軍陳伯之寇淮南，司徒、彭城王勰鎮壽春，以英為鎮南將軍，率眾討之。
manualTranslations.literal: Xiao Baojuan sent his general Chen Bozhi to raid Huainan. The Minister of Works, Xie, Prince of Pengcheng, guarded Shouchun, and Ying was made General Who Guards the South and led troops to attack them.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Xiao Baojuan sent the general Chen Bozhi to raid Huainan, Xie, Prince of Pengcheng and Minister of Works, guarded Shouchun; Ying was made General Who Guards the South and led troops against the invaders.

manualTranslations.zh: 英未至，賊已引退。

manualTranslations.idiomatic: Before Ying arrived, the enemy had already withdrawn.

manualTranslations.zh: 勰還，詔英行揚州。
manualTranslations.literal: When Xie returned, an edict appointed Ying acting governor of Yangzhou.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Xie returned, an edict appointed Ying to act in Yangzhou.

localRange.text: 校勘記魏書卷二十諸本目錄此卷注「闕」字，卷後當有宋人校語，傳本脫去。殿本考證云：「魏收書闕，後人所補。檢傳文除少數字句外與北史卷一九文成五王傳同。孝元皇后生獻文皇帝卷一三后妃傳文成元皇后單諡「元」，卷八三上外戚李峻傳〈補〉、卷八九酷吏李洪之傳補也只稱「元皇后」，唯墓誌集釋元顥妃李元姜墓誌〈圖版一八三〉稱「元恭皇后」，但未見有「孝元」之號，疑「孝」乃「李」字之訛。詮與李平高殖等四面攻燒張森楷北史校勘記云：「高肇傳〈魏書卷八三下，即以北史卷八０補〉『殖』作『植』。按傳稱高植以濟州刺史「率州軍討破元愉，別將有功」，顯與此「高殖」為一人。當時習慣人名地名常通用同音字，但這裏當是「植」字形訛。中書侍郎高聰等議曰諸本「聰」作「敏」。北史卷一九文成五王傳、冊府卷五八０〈六九五七頁〉作「聰」。按卷六八高聰傳，他在太和中自中書博士為侍郎，當時別無「高敏」其人，「敏」字訛，今據改。子靈道襲卒諡悼王墓誌集釋元煥墓誌〈圖版一六一之二〉「靈道」作「靈遵」，這裏「道」字當是「遵」形近而訛。又「悼王」作「哀王」，諸墓誌諡號不但常與史異，而且誌與誌也有不同，未必定是傳誤。子祐字伯授墓誌集釋元祐墓誌「授」作「援」，疑「授」字訛。

sourceRange.text: 齊郡王簡，字叔亮。太和五年封，位中都大官。簡母，沮渠牧犍女也。簡性貌特類外祖。後為內都大官。高祖嘗與簡俱朝文明太后於皇信堂，簡居帝之右，行家人禮。遷太保。高祖仁孝，以諸父零落，存者唯簡。每見，立以待之，俟坐，致敬問起居，停簡拜伏。簡性好酒，不能理公私之事。妻常氏，燕郡公常喜女也，文明太后以賜簡。性幹綜家事，頗節斷簡酒，乃至盜竊，求乞婢侍，卒不能禁。二十三年薨。時高祖不豫，詔曰：「叔父薨背，痛慕摧絕，不自勝任，但虛頓床枕，未堪奉赴，當力疾發哀。」諡曰靈王。世宗時，改諡曰順。子祐，字伯授，襲。母常氏，高祖以納不以禮，不許其為妃。世宗以母從子貴，詔特拜為齊國太妃。祐位涇州刺史。薨，諡曰敬。河間王若，字叔儒。年十六，未封而薨，追封河間，諡曰孝。詔京兆康王子太安為後。太安於若為從弟，非相後之義，廢之，以齊郡王子琛繼。

context.beforeSource: 卒，諡悼王。
context.afterSource: 琛字曇寶，幼而敏慧，高祖愛之。
